1	package datatable
2	
3	import "github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss"
4	
5	// Rule 116: the column widths must sum to exactly the space available, or the
6	// selected row stops short of the right viewport border.
7	//
8	// Every view enforced that the same way — last column absorbs the remainder —
9	// and several then applied a per-column `max(…, floor)` *after* the remainder
10	// was computed, which silently pushes the sum back over. `workspaces` overflows
11	// by 34 columns on a 120-wide terminal that way.
12	//
13	// The fix is not a better clamp. It is to distribute the shortfall across the
14	// columns instead of letting each one defend its own floor: a floor that cannot
15	// be honoured has to be given up by somebody, and deciding that here is what
16	// makes the invariant hold at every width rather than most of them.
17	
18	// borderWidth is the viewport's two vertical borders.
19	const borderWidth = 2
20	
21	// cellPadding is what bubbles/table adds per column — Padding(0, 1).
22	const cellPadding = 2
23	
24	// availableFor returns the width the columns have to share, given the full
25	// viewport width. Negative when the terminal cannot even hold the borders and
26	// the padding, which the solver reads as "no room at all".
27	func availableFor(viewportWidth, numColumns int) int {
28		return viewportWidth - borderWidth - numColumns*cellPadding
29	}
30	
31	// sortArrowWidth is what titleFor appends to the sorted column's header.
32	// Measured rather than assumed: the arrows are not ASCII, and bubbles/table
33	// truncates the header with the same rune widths lipgloss counts.
34	var sortArrowWidth = max(lipgloss.Width(sortArrowAsc), lipgloss.Width(sortArrowDesc))
35	
36	// askFor is the width a column needs, which is not always the MinWidth it
37	// states.
38	//
39	// MinWidth is the view's statement about the column's *content*. A sortable
40	// column also carries a header this package widens by an arrow, and nothing
41	// told the view about those two cells — so a count column asking for 5 rendered
42	// "CRIT ▼" into it and lost exactly the character that says how it is sorted.
43	//
44	// The room is reserved for every sortable column, not only the one currently
45	// sorted: reserving it on demand would resize the column each time `.` moved
46	// the sort, shifting every column beside it.
47	func askFor[T any](c Column[T]) int {
48		width := max(c.MinWidth, 0)
49		if c.Less == nil {
50			return width
51		}
52		return max(width, lipgloss.Width(c.Title)+sortArrowWidth)
53	}
54	
55	// solveWidths distributes available across the columns.
56	//
57	// Fixed columns (Flex == 0) ask for MinWidth. Flexible ones ask for MinWidth
58	// and share whatever is left in proportion to their Flex weight. When there is
59	// not enough for everyone, the shortfall comes out of the flexible columns
60	// first and the fixed ones only after — a fixed column is fixed because its
61	// content has a known size, so it is the last thing worth truncating.
62	//
63	// The result always sums to exactly max(available, 0).
64	func solveWidths[T any](columns []Column[T], available int) []int {
65		widths := make([]int, len(columns))
66		if len(columns) == 0 || available <= 0 {
67			return widths
68		}
69	
70		total := 0
71		for i, c := range columns {
72			widths[i] = askFor(c)
73			total += widths[i]
74		}
75	
76		switch {
77		case total < available:
78			grow(columns, widths, available-total)
79		case total > available:
80			shrink(columns, widths, total-available)
81		}
82		return widths
83	}
84	
85	// grow hands the surplus to the flexible columns by weight, giving the last one
86	// the rounding remainder so the sum is exact. With no flexible column the last
87	// column absorbs it, which is what every view did by hand.
88	func grow[T any](columns []Column[T], widths []int, surplus int) {
89		weight := 0
90		last := -1
91		for i, c := range columns {
92			if c.Flex > 0 {
93				weight += c.Flex
94				last = i
95			}
96		}
97		if weight == 0 {
98			widths[len(widths)-1] += surplus
99			return
100		}
101	
102		given := 0
103		for i, c := range columns {
104			if c.Flex <= 0 || i == last {
105				continue
106			}
107			share := surplus * c.Flex / weight
108			widths[i] += share
109			given += share
110		}
111		widths[last] += surplus - given
112	}
113	
114	// shrink reclaims the shortfall, taking from the flexible columns before the
115	// fixed ones and from the widest before the narrowest, so that one long column
116	// gives way before several short ones become unreadable.
117	func shrink[T any](columns []Column[T], widths []int, shortfall int) {
118		shortfall = takeFrom(widths, order(columns, true), shortfall)
119		takeFrom(widths, order(columns, false), shortfall)
120	}
121	
122	// order returns the column indices to reclaim from, widest first, restricted to
123	// the flexible ones or the fixed ones.
124	func order[T any](columns []Column[T], flexible bool) []int {
125		var idx []int
126		for i, c := range columns {
127			if (c.Flex > 0) == flexible {
128				idx = append(idx, i)
129			}
130		}
131		return idx
132	}
133	
134	// takeFrom removes shortfall from the given columns one unit at a time, always
135	// from the widest, and returns what could not be taken. One unit at a time
136	// keeps it exact and level: no column is emptied while another stays wide.
137	func takeFrom(widths []int, idx []int, shortfall int) int {
138		for shortfall > 0 {
139			widest, at := 0, -1
140			for _, i := range idx {
141				if widths[i] > widest {
142					widest, at = widths[i], i
143				}
144			}
145			if at < 0 {
146				return shortfall // nothing left with any width to give
147			}
148			widths[at]--
149			shortfall--
150		}
151		return 0
152	}

content.text:
Corrigé et poussé sur la [PR #44](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/44).

## La cause

Ce n'était pas les colonnes de l'inventaire, c'était `datatable`. `Column.MinWidth` est ce que la vue dit du **contenu** ; `titleFor` ajoute ensuite une flèche à l'en-tête, et `solveWidths` ignorait ces deux cellules. Le composant élargissait donc en silence ce qu'il était en train de dimensionner. `CRIT` demandait 5 et rendait `CRIT ▼` — 6 — dedans.

Le correctif est dans le composant : `askFor` réserve `width(Title) + sortArrowWidth` pour toute colonne portant un `Less`. Les chaînes de flèches sont des constantes nommées, pour que le rendu et le solveur ne puissent plus diverger.

**Réservé pour toute colonne triable, pas seulement celle qui est triée** — sinon la colonne changerait de largeur à chaque `.` et décalerait toutes ses voisines.

## Portée réelle

J'ai audité toutes les tables en résolvant chaque constante de largeur : `CRIT` et `HIGH` de l'inventaire sont **les deux seules colonnes de l'application** que la réserve modifie. Toutes les autres colonnes triables avaient déjà la place (`Visibility` tombe pile à 12, les autres ont de la marge).

J'ai ensuite fixé les quatre colonnes de comptage à une largeur unique (`countColumnWidth = 6`) : la réserve seule laissait `CRIT`/`HIGH` à 6 et `MED`/`LOW` à 5, soit quatre colonnes adjacentes de même nature en dents de scie.

Rendu vérifié par sonde :

```
 Target ...                       CRIT ▼  HIGH    MED     LOW     Scanned
```

## Vérification

`build`, `vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issue), suite complète au vert. Couverture `datatable` 96.3 %, total projet 81.5 %.

Le test mord : en remettant `askFor` à `MinWidth`, il échoue avec `header "CRIT ▲" is 6 wide in a column of 5 — the arrow is truncated`. J'ai aussi ajouté la forme de l'inventaire à `TestTheWidthsAlwaysSumToWhatIsAvailable` — élever ce qu'une colonne demande est une autre façon de dépasser la place disponible, et Rule 116 doit y survivre à toutes les largeurs de 0 à 200.

content.text:
# Plan Command

This command creates a comprehensive implementation plan before writing any code. It accepts either free-form requirements or a PRD markdown file.

Run inline by default. Do not call the Task tool or any subagent by default. This keeps `/plan` usable from plugin installs that ship commands without agent files.

## What This Command Does

1. **Restate Requirements** - Clarify what needs to be built
2. **Identify Risks** - Surface potential issues and blockers
3. **Create Step Plan** - Break down implementation into phases
4. **Wait for Confirmation** - MUST receive user approval before proceeding

## When to Use

Use `/plan` when:
- Starting a new feature
- Making significant architectural changes
- Working on complex refactoring
- Multiple files/components will be affected
- Requirements are unclear or ambiguous

## How It Works

The assistant will:

1. **Analyze the request** and restate requirements in clear terms
2. **Ground the plan** in relevant codebase patterns when the repo is available
3. **Break down into phases** with specific, actionable steps
4. **Identify dependencies** between components
5. **Assess risks** and potential blockers
6. **Estimate complexity** (High/Medium/Low)
7. **Present the plan** and WAIT for your explicit confirmation

## Input Modes

| Input | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path/to/name.prd.md` | PRD artifact mode | Read the PRD, pick the next pending delivery milestone or implementation phase, and write `.claude/plans/{name}.plan.md` |
| Any other markdown path | Reference mode | Read the file as context and produce an inline plan |
| Free-form text | Conversational mode | Produce an inline plan |
| Empty input | Clarification mode | Ask what should be planned |

In PRD artifact mode, create `.claude/plans/` if needed. If the PRD contains a `Delivery Milestones` table, update only the selected row from `pending` to `in-progress` and set its `Plan` cell to the generated plan path. If the PRD uses the legacy `.claude/PRPs/prds/` format with `Implementation Phases`, read it without migrating paths.

## Pattern Grounding

Before writing the plan, search the codebase for conventions the implementation should mirror. Capture the top example for each relevant category with file references:

| Category | What to capture |
|---|---|
| Naming | File, function, type, command, or script naming in the affected area |
| Error handling | How failures are raised, returned, logged, or handled gracefully |
| Logging | Levels, format, and what gets logged |
| Data access | Repository, service, query, or filesystem patterns |
| Tests | Test file location, framework, fixtures, and assertion style |

If no similar code exists, state that explicitly. Do not invent a pattern.

## PRD Artifact Output

When called with a `.prd.md` file, write the plan to `.claude/plans/{kebab-case-name}.plan.md` using this structure:

````markdown
# Plan: {Feature Name}

**Source PRD**: {path}
**Selected Milestone**: {milestone or phase name}
**Complexity**: {Small | Medium | Large}

## Summary
{2-3 sentences}

## Patterns to Mirror
| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Errors | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Tests | `path:line` | {short description} |

## Files to Change
| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE | {reason} |

## Tasks
### Task 1: {name}
- **Action**: {what to do}
- **Mirror**: {pattern to follow}
- **Validate**: {command that proves correctness}

## Validation
```bash
{project-specific validation commands}
```

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

## Acceptance
- [ ] All tasks complete
- [ ] Validation passes
- [ ] Patterns mirrored, not reinvented
````

After writing the artifact, report its path and WAIT for confirmation before writing code.

## Example Usage

```
User: /plan I need to add real-time notifications when markets resolve

Assistant:
# Implementation Plan: Real-Time Market Resolution Notifications

## Requirements Restatement
- Send notifications to users when markets they're watching resolve
- Support multiple notification channels (in-app, email, webhook)
- Ensure notifications are delivered reliably
- Include market outcome and user's position result

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Database Schema
- Add notifications table with columns: id, user_id, market_id, type, status, created_at
- Add user_notification_preferences table for channel preferences
- Create indexes on user_id and market_id for performance

### Phase 2: Notification Service
- Create notification service in lib/notifications.ts
- Implement notification queue using BullMQ/Redis
- Add retry logic for failed deliveries
- Create notification templates

### Phase 3: Integration Points
- Hook into market resolution logic (when status changes to "resolved")
- Query all users with positions in market
- Enqueue notifications for each user

### Phase 4: Frontend Components
- Create NotificationBell component in header
- Add NotificationList modal
- Implement real-time updates via Supabase subscriptions
- Add notification preferences page

## Dependencies
- Redis (for queue)
- Email service (SendGrid/Resend)
- Supabase real-time subscriptions

## Risks
- HIGH: Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM required)
- MEDIUM: Performance with 1000+ users per market
- MEDIUM: Notification spam if markets resolve frequently
- LOW: Real-time subscription overhead

## Estimated Complexity: MEDIUM
- Backend: 4-6 hours
- Frontend: 3-4 hours
- Testing: 2-3 hours
- Total: 9-13 hours

**WAITING FOR CONFIRMATION**: Proceed with this plan? (yes/no/modify)
```

## Important Notes

**CRITICAL**: This command will **NOT** write any code until you explicitly confirm the plan with "yes" or "proceed" or similar affirmative response.

If you want changes, respond with:
- "modify: [your changes]"
- "different approach: [alternative]"
- "skip phase 2 and do phase 3 first"

## Integration with Other Commands

After planning:
- Use the `tdd-workflow` skill to implement with test-driven development
- Use `/build-fix` if build errors occur
- Use `/code-review` to review completed implementation
- Use `/pr` or `/prp-pr` to open a pull request

> **Need requirements first?** Use `/plan-prd` for a lean PRD at `.claude/prds/{name}.prd.md`.
>
> **Need the legacy PRP flow?** Use `/prp-plan` for deep PRP planning with `.claude/PRPs/` artifacts. Use `/prp-implement` to execute those plans with rigorous validation loops.

## Optional Planner Agent

ECC also provides a `planner` agent for manual installs that include agent files. Use it only when the local runtime already exposes that subagent and the user explicitly asks you to delegate planning.

If the `planner` subagent is unavailable, continue planning inline instead of surfacing an "Agent type 'planner' not found" error.

For manual installs, the source file lives at:
`agents/planner.md`

11-//
12-// ScanOptions used to be assembled by hand in three places — the security form,
13-// the workspaces list and the images list — and the three had drifted:
14-// IgnoreEOL was set in one of them, so ticking "ignore EOL" applied when
15-// scanning from the form and silently did not when scanning from either list.
16-//
17-// So this does not assert that IgnoreEOL is carried. It asserts that *every*
18-// field the two structs have in common is carried, by walking them: a tenth
19-// option added to ScanConfig and ScanOptions without plumbing it through fails
20-// here rather than shipping.

28-	cfgValue := reflect.ValueOf(&cfg).Elem()
29-	for _, name := range shared {
30-		cfgValue.FieldByName(name).Set(distinctValue(name, cfgValue.FieldByName(name).Type()))

content.text:
J'ai relevé toute la surface. Voici le plan — **je n'écris rien avant ton accord**.

---

# Plan : supprimer la génération de SBOM

## Reformulation

Supprimer entièrement la fonctionnalité SBOM : les deux réglages de configuration, l'étage de scan, les constructeurs de commande Trivy, les deux contrôles d'interface, le champ porté par le résultat, et la documentation. Aucun vestige inerte : ni option réglable et non lue, ni fonction sans appelant.

## Ce que j'ai constaté

| Fait | Conséquence |
|---|---|
| `Result.SBOMPath` est **écrit par l'étage SBOM et lu par personne** | L'aide affirme « If SBOM was generated, its path is shown above the tabs » — c'est faux aujourd'hui. Rien à remplacer, juste à retirer. |
| `config.Load` utilise `yaml.Unmarshal` sans `KnownFields(true)` | `generate_sbom:` et `sbom_output_dir:` déjà présents dans les fichiers utilisateurs sont **ignorés en silence** puis disparaissent au premier `config.Save()`. **Aucune migration nécessaire.** |
| `Result` est sérialisé en JSON dans le cache de scan | `encoding/json` ignore les champs inconnus : un rapport en cache portant `sbom_path` se relit sans erreur. Idem, pas de migration. |
| `containerOutputPath` n'est utilisé que par `sbomArgs` | Meurt avec lui. |
| `dockerSocketMount` est aussi utilisé par `wrapTrivy` | **Survit** — ne pas le supprimer avec le reste. |
| `applyServerModeConstraints` existe **en double** (formulaire + vue config) | Les deux doivent perdre leur ligne SBOM, sinon elles divergent. |
| `SBOMComponent` cité dans les codemaps **n'existe nulle part dans le code** | Obsolescence préexistante des codemaps, pas causée par ce changement. Je la corrige au passage. |

## Motifs à respecter

| Catégorie | Source | Motif |
|---|---|---|
| Suppression avec l'appelant | `docs/backlog.md` §1.1 (`:theme`, `RenderRadioButton`) | Le code mort part avec son dernier appelant, dans le même commit, chiffré dans le message |
| Champs de configuration | `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:218` | Une table de `field`, un accesseur pointeur par réglage |
| Contrainte serveur | `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go:277` | `serverModeFields`, table indexée par libellé |
| Tests de plomberie | `internal/scan/options_test.go:21` | `TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` marche les noms de champs partagés — se réajuste seul |

## Phases

### Phase 1 — `internal/scan` : le cœur

| Fichier | Action |
|---|---|
| `scanner.go` | Retirer `ScanOptions.GenerateSBOM`, `ScanOptions.SBOMOutputDir`, `Result.SBOMPath`, l'étage SBOM entier (`Scan`), le `\|\| s.options.GenerateSBOM` de `missingToolErrors`, et les deux commentaires qui citent `sbom` |
| `options.go` | Retirer les deux affectations |
| `trivy.go` | Supprimer `GetSBOMCommand` et `GenerateSBOM` |
| `trivy_args.go` | Supprimer `sbomArgs`, `sbomSubcommand`, `sbomFileName`, la constante `containerOutputPath`, et l'import `path/filepath` devenu inutile (`strings` survit, ligne 53) |

### Phase 2 — configuration

| Fichier | Action |
|---|---|
| `config/config.go` | Retirer `GenerateSBOM`, `SBOMOutputDir`, et la ligne `expand` associée |
| `configuration/fields.go` | Retirer la bascule « Generate SBOM », le champ texte « SBOM output dir », l'entrée de `serverModeFields`, et reformuler la description de « Trivy server » (« disables misconfig, license and SBOM » → sans SBOM) |
| `configuration/update.go` | Retirer la ligne de `applyServerModeConstraints` |

### Phase 3 — le formulaire security *(la phase risquée)*

Le formulaire meurt en phase 3 du plan configuration-view, mais il vit encore. Retirer sa case coche **renumérote tous les indices au-dessus de 6** :

```
avant : 6=sbom  7=trivyServer  8=ignoreUnfixed  9=ignoreEOL  10=gitleaksConfig  11=history  12=bouton
après :         6=trivyServer  7=ignoreUnfixed  8=ignoreEOL   9=gitleaksConfig  10=history  11=bouton
```

Touche `model.go` (champ `generateSBOM`, son init, les indices de `InEditMode`), `form.go` (`totalFields` 13→12, `isServerIncompatibleField`, `isTextInputField`, `focusTextField`, `applyServerModeConstraints`, `saveOptionsToConfig`), `view.go` (la case, les indices de la colonne droite, `renderStartButton`, la note mode serveur), `header.go` (l'aide), `warnings.go` (le préfixe `"sbom generation failed: "`).

### Phase 4 — tests

Suppression : ~9 tests SBOM dédiés (`command_test.go`, `execute_test.go`). Ajustement : `scan_test.go` (branche `stageOf`, `everyStage()`, 4 scripts d'étage, assertions `SBOMPath`, listes d'étages attendues, **6 erreurs → 5**), `configuration/model_test.go`, `security/model_test.go` (mode serveur + table indice→bascule), `security/view_test.go`, `security/warnings_test.go`.

### Phase 5 — documentation

`.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `README.md`, `docs/CODEMAPS/{backend,data,dependencies}.md`, plus une entrée `docs/backlog.md`.

## Validation

```bash
go build ./... && go vet ./...
mise run lint          # doit rester à 0 issue
go test ./...
grep -rin "sbom" --include=*.go .          # attendu : vide
go test ./... -coverprofile=/tmp/c.out && go tool cover -func=/tmp/c.out | tail -1
```

Plus une vérification manuelle : un `config.yaml` portant `generate_sbom: true` doit charger sans erreur.

## Risques

| Risque | Probabilité | Atténuation |
|---|---|---|
| **La renumérotation du formulaire casse la navigation en silence** | Élevée | `TestFieldNavigationWraps`, `TestTextFieldsTakeFocusOnArrival`, `TestSpaceTogglesEachCheckbox` et la table indice→bascule couvrent exactement ça. Je les fais échouer d'abord pour vérifier qu'ils mordent. |
| Une seule des deux `applyServerModeConstraints` est corrigée | Moyenne | Les deux sont nommées explicitement en phases 2 et 3 |
| `dockerSocketMount` supprimé par erreur avec `containerOutputPath` | Moyenne | Le build casse immédiatement (`wrapTrivy`) |
| Baisse de couverture | Faible | Le SBOM est très couvert ; sa suppression retire code **et** tests. Je mesure avant/après. |

## Deux choix que j'assume, dis-moi si tu préfères autrement

1. **Je ne réécris pas `docs/backlog.md:557`**, qui cite `sbomArgs` dans le récit d'un correctif passé. C'est un enregistrement historique ; j'ajoute une entrée pour la suppression plutôt que de réécrire ce qui a eu lieu. La contrepartie est une référence à une fonction disparue.
2. **Je renumérote le formulaire plutôt que d'anticiper sa suppression** (phase 3 du plan configuration-view). Le supprimer maintenant dépasse la demande.

**Complexité : moyenne.** ~25 fichiers, mécanique sur 90 %, avec la renumérotation comme seul endroit où une erreur passerait inaperçue sans les tests.

---

**Why after phase 3** (the deletion of `internal/ui/security/form.go`, per
[`configuration-view-plan.md`](../.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md)) and
not before: the form addresses its fields by index, and SBOM is index 6 of
thirteen. Removing it now renumbers everything above it —

```
before : 6=sbom  7=trivyServer  8=ignoreUnfixed  9=ignoreEOL  10=gitleaksConfig  11=history  12=button
after  :         6=trivyServer  7=ignoreUnfixed  8=ignoreEOL   9=gitleaksConfig  10=history  11=button
```

— across `totalFields`, `isServerIncompatibleField`, `isTextInputField`,
`focusTextField`, `Model.InEditMode`, the space-toggle switch, the right column

Consigné en **`docs/backlog.md` §3.14**, avec les renvois dans le plan. Aucun code touché.

## Pourquoi après la phase 3 — la raison est écrite noir sur blanc

Le formulaire adresse ses champs par indice et le SBOM est l'indice 6 sur treize. Le supprimer maintenant décale sept champs à travers `totalFields`, `isServerIncompatibleField`, `isTextInputField`, `focusTextField`, `InEditMode`, le switch de bascule, la colonne droite de `renderInputView`, `renderStartButton` et les tests qui épinglent ces indices — travail intégralement jeté quand la phase 3 supprime le fichier. Différer fait disparaître toute cette phase.

## Ce que l'entrée conserve du relevé

La table des suppressions par fichier, et les six points qui n'auront pas à être redécouverts :

1. **`Result.SBOMPath` est écrit par l'étage et lu par personne.** L'aide affirme que le chemin est affiché au-dessus des onglets — c'est faux aujourd'hui, indépendamment de la suppression.
2. **Aucune migration** : `config.Load` utilise `yaml.Unmarshal` sans `KnownFields`, donc `generate_sbom:` est ignoré puis disparaît au premier `Save`. Les rapports en cache sont du JSON, même comportement.
3. **`containerOutputPath` meurt avec `sbomArgs`, `dockerSocketMount` doit survivre** — `wrapTrivy` s'en sert. Les supprimer ensemble est l'erreur facile.
4. **`applyServerModeConstraints` existe en double** ; seule la copie de la vue configuration survit à la phase 3.
5. **`TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` ne demande aucune retouche** — il marche les noms de champs partagés, donc c'est lui qui échoue si un seul côté est fait.
6. Les codemaps décrivent un type `SBOMComponent` qui **n'existe nulle part**. Obsolescence préexistante, à retirer avec le reste.

Plus la liste nominative des tests à supprimer et à ajuster (dont le compte d'erreurs par étage qui passe de 6 à 5), la doc à toucher, et les commandes de validation.

## Ajouté au plan au passage

La phase 3 gagne le tableau des **trois champs qui meurent avec le formulaire et seulement avec lui** — `homeState`, `deps` (dont j'avais retiré le dernier lecteur hors formulaire en refaisant le header) et les miroirs d'options. C'était dispersé dans mes messages ; c'est maintenant à l'endroit où on le lira.

J'ai vérifié que chaque symbole et chaque test cités dans l'entrée existent bien dans le code — pas de référence morte à la rédaction. Un point de fragilité assumé : ces noms dériveront si le code bouge d'ici la phase 3, mais ils sont greppables, ce que des numéros de ligne n'auraient pas été.

1	package app
2	
3	import (
4		"log"
5	
6		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
7	
8		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/gitlab/explorer"
10		ociresources "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/oci_resources"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/security"
12		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/workspaces"
13	)
14	
15	// Selection mode lets one view borrow another to pick something — a scan
16	// target, a clone destination. The router remembers where to come back to and
17	// translates the answer into the message the borrower understands.
18	
19	// pullDestinationPrompt is shown while the explorer borrows the workspaces view.
20	const pullDestinationPrompt = "Enter into a parent directory — the repo will be cloned inside it"
21	
22	// handleSelectionRequest switches to workspaces or oci_resources in selection mode
23	func (a *App) handleSelectionRequest(msg security.SelectionRequestMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
24		a.selectionReturnView = a.currentView
25	
26		switch msg.Type {
27		case "directory":
28			log.Printf("Selection request: switching to workspaces for directory selection")
29			return a, a.openBrowser(command.ViewWorkspaces, workspaces.NewForSelection(a.config, msg.Message))
30		case "image":
31			log.Printf("Selection request: switching to OCI images for image selection")
32			return a, a.openBrowser(command.ViewOCIResources, ociresources.NewForSelection(a.config, msg.Message))
33		}
34		return a, nil
35	}
36	
37	// handleExplorerPullRequest borrows the workspaces view to pick a clone target.
38	func (a *App) handleExplorerPullRequest() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
39		a.selectionReturnView = a.currentView
40		log.Printf("Explorer pull request: switching to workspaces for directory selection")
41		return a, a.openBrowser(
42			command.ViewWorkspaces,
43			workspaces.NewForSelection(a.config, pullDestinationPrompt),
44		)
45	}
46	
47	// openBrowser installs a view built in selection mode and lays it out.
48	func (a *App) openBrowser(view command.ViewType, model tea.Model) tea.Cmd {
49		a.views[view] = model
50		a.currentView = view
51		return tea.Batch(model.Init(), a.requestResize())
52	}
53	
54	// handleDirectorySelected returns to the originating view with the chosen path.
55	func (a *App) handleDirectorySelected(msg workspaces.DirectorySelectedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
56		log.Printf("Directory selected: %s, returning to %s", msg.Path, a.selectionReturnView)
57		a.leaveSelectionMode()
58	
59		var result tea.Msg = security.SelectionResultMsg{Path: msg.Path}
60		if a.selectionReturnView == command.ViewGitlabExplorer {
61			result = explorer.PullDestinationSelectedMsg{Path: msg.Path}
62		}
63		return a, a.returnToOrigin(result)
64	}
65	
66	// handleImageSelected returns to the security view with the chosen image.
67	func (a *App) handleImageSelected(msg ociresources.ImageSelectedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
68		log.Printf("Image selected: %s, returning to %s", msg.ImageName, a.selectionReturnView)
69		a.currentView = a.selectionReturnView
70		a.resetSelectionModeFor(command.ViewOCIResources)
71	
72		return a, a.returnToOrigin(security.SelectionResultMsg{Path: msg.ImageName})
73	}
74	
75	// handleSelectionCancelled returns to the originating view without changes.
76	func (a *App) handleSelectionCancelled() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
77		log.Printf("Selection cancelled, returning to %s", a.selectionReturnView)
78		a.leaveSelectionMode()
79	
80		var cancel tea.Msg = security.SelectionCancelledMsg{}
81		if a.selectionReturnView == command.ViewGitlabExplorer {
82			cancel = explorer.PullSelectionCancelledMsg{}
83		}
84		return a, a.returnToOrigin(cancel)
85	}
86	
87	// leaveSelectionMode takes both borrowable views out of it. Workspaces is
88	// dropped so it is rebuilt normally; the OCI view is reset in place because it
89	// holds scan results worth keeping.
90	func (a *App) leaveSelectionMode() {
91		a.currentView = a.selectionReturnView
92		delete(a.views, command.ViewWorkspaces)
93		a.resetSelectionModeFor(command.ViewOCIResources)
94	}
95	
96	// returnToOrigin delivers the outcome to the view that asked and lays it out.
97	func (a *App) returnToOrigin(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
98		view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]
99		if !ok {
100			return nil
101		}
102		updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
103		a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView
104		a.viewport.GotoTop()
105		return tea.Batch(cmd, a.requestResize())
106	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"log"
6	
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
8		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"

10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/scan"
11		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
12	)
13	
14	// Update handles messages
15	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
16		// Handle confirm modal messages first (before passing to modal)
17		switch msg := msg.(type) {
18		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
19			// User confirmed to ignore the secret
20			if m.findingToIgnore != nil {
21				finding := *m.findingToIgnore
22				targetDir := m.targetPath
23				m.confirmModal = nil
24				m.findingToIgnore = nil
25				return m, func() tea.Msg {
26					err := scan.AddToGitleaksIgnore(targetDir, finding)
27					return SecretIgnoredMsg{Finding: finding, Error: err}
28				}
29			}
30			m.confirmModal = nil
31			m.findingToIgnore = nil
32			return m, nil
33	
34		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
35			// User cancelled
36			m.confirmModal = nil
37			m.findingToIgnore = nil
38			return m, nil
39	
40		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
41			m.width = msg.Width
42			m.height = msg.Height
43			// Widths and height in one call; SetHeight accounts for the header row
44			// internally, so m.height goes through as it is. Rows no longer depend
45			// on the width — bubbles truncates each cell to its own column — so
46			// there is nothing to rebuild here.
47			m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
48			m.inventory.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
49			// Update details viewport size and refresh content
50			m.detailsViewport.Width = msg.Width
51			m.detailsViewport.Height = msg.Height
52			if m.state == StateDetails {
53				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
54			}
55			return m, nil
56	
57		case tea.KeyMsg:
58			// Pass key messages to confirm modal if active
59			if m.confirmModal != nil {
60				var cmd tea.Cmd
61				m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
62				return m, cmd
63			}
64			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
65	
66		case DepsCheckedMsg:
67			m.deps = msg.Deps
68			return m, nil
69	
70		case ScanCompleteMsg:
71			return m.handleScanComplete(msg)
72	
73		case SecretIgnoredMsg:
74			if msg.Error != nil {
75				log.Printf("ERROR [security] ignore secret %s: %v", msg.Finding.File, msg.Error)
76				m.statusMessage = "Failed to ignore secret — check logs"
77			} else {
78				m.statusMessage = fmt.Sprintf("Added %s to .gitleaksignore", msg.Finding.File)
79			}
80			return m, clearStatusCmd()
81	
82		case clearStatusMsg:
83			m.statusMessage = ""
84			return m, nil
85	
86		case SelectionResultMsg:
87			m.targetPath = msg.Path
88			m.targetInput.SetValue(msg.Path)
89			return m, nil
90	
91		case SelectionCancelledMsg:
92			return m, nil
93	
94		case StartScanMsg:
95			return m.startScan()
96	
97		case ScanProgressMsg:
98			return m.handleScanProgress(msg)
99	
100		case InventoryLoadedMsg:
101			return m.handleInventoryLoaded(msg)
102	
103		case InventoryResultLoadedMsg:
104			return m.handleInventoryResultLoaded(msg)
105	
106		case InventoryScanFinishedMsg:
107			return m.handleInventoryScanFinished(msg)
108	
109		case spinner.TickMsg:
110			return m.handleSpinnerTick(msg)
111		}
112	
113		return m, nil
114	}
115	
116	// handleSpinnerTick advances the spinner while something is actually spinning.
117	//
118	// The inventory counts as spinning too: its frame is a table cell rather than a
119	// scanning screen, and a frame that never advances reads as a hung scan. Its
120	// rows carry the frame, so they are restamped — but only then, since SetItems
121	// re-filters and re-sorts and there is no reason to do that sixty times a second
122	// for a table with nothing running.
123	func (m Model) handleSpinnerTick(msg spinner.TickMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
124		scanningInventory := m.inventoryScanning()
125		if m.state != StateScanning && !scanningInventory {
126			return m, nil
127		}

destination, and that is all. So `ociresources.NewForSelection`,
`ImageSelectedMsg`, `SelectionCancelledMsg`, `ResetSelectionMsg` and the OCI
view's `selectionMode` are gone, and `app/selection.go` is no longer
parameterised over who is borrowing.

scanned row asks the router for the result file; when it is gone,
`rescanInOrigin` hands `workspaces.ScanRequestMsg` or
`ociresources.ScanRequestMsg` to that list and stays there — the target lives
there, and so does the scan that replaces it. It used to open the form with the
target filled in. Both message types were declared and unhandled before this;
they have handlers now, which is what they were named for.

`LaunchBatchScanMsg`, `LaunchSingleImageScanMsg` and `app.handleLaunchScan` went
with the form: they carried the *options* the form had collected to whoever
would run the scan, and the options come from the configuration view now.

1	# A configuration view, and `security` becomes an inventory
2	
3	Status: **complete.** All five phases shipped. What is left is the SBOM removal
4	that was deliberately deferred until after phase 3 -- `docs/backlog.md` §3.14.
5	
6	| Phase | State |
7	|---|---|
8	| 0 — `IgnoreEOL` (D26) | shipped |
9	| 0b — per-context scan caches | shipped |
10	| 0c — tool source and paths (D27) | shipped |
11	| 1 — configuration view | shipped |
12	| 2 — the inventory | shipped, alongside the form |
13	| 3 — deleting the form | **shipped** |
14	| after 3 — removing SBOM generation | **outstanding**, see `docs/backlog.md` §3.14 |
15	
16	## What was decided
17	
18	| Question | Answer |
19	|---|---|
20	| Scope of the config view | **Scalars only.** The ~29 simple fields. Lists — monitors, registries — stay where they are consulted. |
21	| Fate of `security` | **Inventory of what has been scanned.** `:sec` opens a unified images + workspaces table read from the two caches. |
22	| Free-target picker (`b`) | **Removed.** What gets scanned is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`. |
23	| Scope of a configuration | **Per context.** One config per context, as today; the view edits the current one and must name it. |
24	| Reaching a result from its row | **Preserved.** `enter` on a scanned image or repository opens the findings, `esc` returns to that row. |
25	| `secret_backend` changed at runtime | **Re-resolve, confirm first, migrate nothing.** See below. |
26	
27	## The fact this plan rests on
28	
29	The flow being proposed is already 80 % built, and nobody noticed because the
30	form kept standing in front of it.
31	
32	```go
33	// internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:143
34	func (m Model) getScanOptions() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }
35	
36	// internal/ui/oci_resources/images.go:79
37	func (m Model) defaultScanOpts() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }
38	```
39	
40	Byte-for-byte identical, both reading the config. `ctrl+s` on an image or on a
41	repository has not gone through the security form for some time. And
42	`NewWithPreloadedResult` already opens straight on `StateResults`.
43	
44	So this is not a redesign. It is deleting the one remaining path that reads
45	something *other* than the config, and giving `:sec` a landing page that is not
46	an empty form.
47	
48	---
49	
50	## Phase 0 — D26: `IgnoreEOL` is dropped on two of the three scan paths
51	
52	Independent of everything else, and a real defect. Do it first, alone.
53	
54	`internal/ui/security/scan.go:42` is the third options builder and it is not
55	identical to the other two:
56	
57	```go
58	IgnoreEOL: m.ignoreEOL,   // ← set here, and nowhere else
59	```
60	
61	The option is persisted to `config.Scan.IgnoreEOL` by the form, and wired all
62	the way through to `--ignore-status end_of_life` in `scanner.go:340`. Neither
63	`getScanOptions` nor `defaultScanOpts` sets it. Tick "ignore EOL", scan from the
64	images list, the flag silently does not apply.
65	
66	Three copies, one divergent — the same shape as D24 and D25, which §2 closed
67	nine times over in the tables.
68	
69	**Fix.** One builder, and delete the other three:
70	
71	```go
72	// internal/scan/options.go
73	// OptionsFromConfig is the only way scan options are built. Three call sites
74	// used to assemble them by hand and one of them set IgnoreEOL (D26).
75	func OptionsFromConfig(c config.ScanConfig) ScanOptions
76	```
77	
78	`internal/scan` does not import `internal/config` today and `internal/config`
79	does not import `internal/scan`, so this direction is acyclic. Verified.
80	
81	**Test that bites first.** Assert `OptionsFromConfig` carries every field of
82	`ScanConfig` that `ScanOptions` has a home for — a table over the field names,
83	so adding a tenth option to the config without plumbing it fails the test rather
84	than shipping. This is the class of defect, not the instance.
85	
86	---
87	
88	## Phase 0c — D27: the custom tool paths are never read, and the source cannot be chosen
89	
90	Independent of the config view, but a prerequisite for its `scan` section being
91	honest about what it offers.
92	
93	### The defect
94	
95	`trivy_path` and `gitleaks_path` are declared, defaulted and tilde-expanded, and
96	**nothing reads them**:
97	
98	```
99	config.go:119   TrivyPath string `yaml:"trivy_path"`   // declared
100	config.go:302   TrivyPath: ""                          // defaulted
101	config.go:491   c.Scan.TrivyPath = expand(…)           // expanded on load
102	                                                       // ← and that is all
103	scanner.go:207  exec.LookPath("trivy")                 // hard-coded
104	scanner.go:210  exec.Command("trivy", "--version")     // hard-coded
105	gitleaks.go:73  toolCmd{Name: "gitleaks"}              // hard-coded
106	```
107	
108	Setting `trivy_path: /opt/trivy/bin/trivy` does nothing, silently. Somebody
109	thought the field mattered — it is expanded on load — and no reader was ever
110	written.
111	
112	### The half that goes with it
113	
114	`CheckDependenciesWithImages` resolves the binary first and only reaches for
115	Docker in the `else`. A binary on `PATH` therefore always wins, so a user who
116	wants the pinned image cannot have it while Trivy is installed.
117	
118	"Either the image or the binary" needs a **choice**, not two fields configured
119	in the hope that the right one is picked.
120	
121	### What ships
122	
123	New per-tool source setting, `auto` by default so existing configs behave
124	identically:
125	
126	```yaml
127	scan:
128	  trivy_source: auto      # auto | binary | image
129	  trivy_path: ""
130	  trivy_image: aquasec/trivy
131	  gitleaks_source: auto
132	```
133	
134	| Value | Resolution |
135	|---|---|
136	| `auto` | today's behaviour — the binary if present, else the image |
137	| `binary` | `trivy_path` when set, else `trivy` from `PATH`. **Fails loudly when absent**, never falls back to Docker |
138	| `image` | `trivy_image`, even when a binary is on `PATH` |
139	
140	The loud failure is the point. The silent fallback to Docker is what has kept
141	D27 invisible: scans keep working, with something other than what was asked for.
142	
143	Plumbing:
144	
145	- `CheckDependenciesWithImages(trivyImage, gitleaksImage)` takes only the
146	  images. It needs the paths and the preference — replace it with one that takes
147	  `config.ScanConfig`, alongside `OptionsFromConfig` from phase 0.
148	- `DependencyStatus` gains `TrivyBinary` / `GitleaksBinary` next to the existing
149	  `TrivyImage` / `GitleaksImage`.
150	- `GetTrivyCommand` already takes 8 positional arguments. Pass the whole
151	  `DependencyStatus` rather than adding a ninth — the argument list is why the
152	  binary path was never threaded through in the first place.
153	
154	**Test that bites first.** A `trivy_source: image` config must produce a Docker
155	command even with a fake `trivy` on `PATH`, and `trivy_source: binary` with a
156	non-existent path must return an error rather than a Docker command.
157	
158	## Phase 1 — the configuration view
159	
160	Additive. Nothing is removed in this phase, so it ships green on its own.
161	
162	### Fields
163	
164	~29 scalars across five sections. Everything not listed is a list and stays put.
165	
166	| Section | Fields |
167	|---|---|
168	| `app` | `theme`, `default_view`, `workspaces_dir`, `ide_command`, `terminal_command`, `secret_backend`, `log_file` |
169	| `gitlab` | `url`, `default_parent_group`, `default_visibility`, `clone_method`, `pull.target_dir`, `pull.parallel_jobs`, `pull.max_depth`, `pull.include_archived` |
170	| `scan` | the 9 option booleans, `trivy_source` + `trivy_path` + `trivy_image`, `gitleaks_source` + `gitleaks_path` + `gitleaks_image`, `trivy_server`, `gitleaks_config`, `sbom_output_dir`, `timeout`, `max_concurrent_scans`, `max_cached_reports` |
171	| `docker` | `network_tool_image` |
172	| `status` | `refresh_interval`, `timeout`, `auto_refresh` |
173	
174	`secret_backend` is the field that justifies the view on its own: a documented
175	security decision, three values, a fallback — and the only way to change it
176	today is to open a YAML file.
177

### 3.15 The scan form is deleted (phase 3) — **done**

The last phase of
[`configuration-view-plan.md`](../.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md).
2 538 lines removed against 530 added, across 32 files.

Both prerequisites had landed: `applyServerModeConstraints` lives in the
configuration view's `update.go`, and `scan.ValidateTrivyServer` is wired to its
`trivy_server` field.

**`StateScanning` went with `StateInput`**, which the plan did not anticipate.
`startScan` had two callers — the form, and the router's image fallback — and
once both were gone the whole in-place scanning machinery had no user:
the progress channel, `scanGen`, `cancelScan`, `waitForProgressCmd`,
`purgeScanCacheCmd`, `ScanCompleteMsg`, `ScanProgressMsg`, `StartScanMsg`. The
inventory rescans in the background with a spinner on the row (§3.11), so
nothing waits on a whole screen for one target. `scan.go` emptied out except
`hasScanSource`, which moved next to its one remaining caller.

**Three fields died with the form**, as recorded in the plan: `homeState` (the
inventory is the only landing state left, so `goHome` stopped branching), `deps`
with `checkDependencies` and `DepsCheckedMsg` (the Start button was its last
reader, the header having stopped showing tool versions in §3.12), and the ~15
option mirrors.

**The browser bridge went at both ends.** The form borrowed the workspaces view
for a directory and the images view for an image; the explorer borrows the
workspaces view for a clone destination, and that is the only borrow left. So
`app/selection.go` stopped being parameterised over who is borrowing, and the
images view lost `NewForSelection`, `ImageSelectedMsg`, `SelectionCancelledMsg`,
`ResetSelectionMsg`, `selectionMode` and the six render sites that read it.
`resetSelectionModeFor` collapsed to dropping one view.

**A missing stored result now rescans in the list it came from.** `enter` on a
scanned row asks the router for the result file; when it is gone,
`rescanInOrigin` hands the target's name to that list and stays there, rather
than opening a security view on nothing. `workspaces.ScanRequestMsg` and
`ociresources.ScanRequestMsg` were **declared and unhandled** before this — dead
types carrying exactly the right shape — and they have handlers now.
`LaunchBatchScanMsg`, `LaunchSingleImageScanMsg` and `handleLaunchScan` went with
the form: they carried the options it had collected, and options come from the
configuration view.

**Coverage.** The deleted tests were covering live code incidentally, and two
regressions had to be repaired rather than accepted: the explorer's borrow
(`handleDirectorySelected`, `leaveSelectionMode`, `returnToOrigin` all fell to
0 %, exercised only by the security selection tests that went) and
`openSecurityView` (the two result handlers' success path). Both have their own
tests now, as do the two `ScanRequestMsg` handlers, `Init`, `handleSpinnerTick`
and the details viewport's scrolling. `internal/ui/security` 86.5 % → 87.2 %,
`internal/app` unchanged at 87.0 %, **no package lower than before**; project
total 81.5 % → 81.4 %, the residue of deleting a well-covered package's code.

`internal/ui/security/scan_test.go` was deleted whole. Its two durable
invariants live elsewhere: `ValidateTrivyServer` refusing `":"` is
`internal/scan/command_test.go`, and `alt+:` reaching the router rather than a
text field is `internal/app/command_mode_test.go`.

### 3.15 The scan form is deleted (phase 3) — **done**

The last phase of
[`configuration-view-plan.md`](../.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md).
2 538 lines removed against 530 added, across 32 files.

Both prerequisites had landed: `applyServerModeConstraints` lives in the
configuration view's `update.go`, and `scan.ValidateTrivyServer` is wired to its
`trivy_server` field.

**`StateScanning` went with `StateInput`**, which the plan did not anticipate.
`startScan` had two callers — the form, and the router's image fallback — and
once both were gone the whole in-place scanning machinery had no user:
the progress channel, `scanGen`, `cancelScan`, `waitForProgressCmd`,
`purgeScanCacheCmd`, `ScanCompleteMsg`, `ScanProgressMsg`, `StartScanMsg`. The
inventory rescans in the background with a spinner on the row (§3.11), so
nothing waits on a whole screen for one target. `scan.go` emptied out except
`hasScanSource`, which moved next to its one remaining caller.

**Three fields died with the form**, as recorded in the plan: `homeState` (the
inventory is the only landing state left, so `goHome` stopped branching), `deps`
with `checkDependencies` and `DepsCheckedMsg` (the Start button was its last
reader, the header having stopped showing tool versions in §3.12), and the ~15
option mirrors.

**The browser bridge went at both ends.** The form borrowed the workspaces view
for a directory and the images view for an image; the explorer borrows the
workspaces view for a clone destination, and that is the only borrow left. So
`app/selection.go` stopped being parameterised over who is borrowing, and the
images view lost `NewForSelection`, `ImageSelectedMsg`, `SelectionCancelledMsg`,
`ResetSelectionMsg`, `selectionMode` and the six render sites that read it.
`resetSelectionModeFor` collapsed to dropping one view.

**A missing stored result now rescans in the list it came from.** `enter` on a
scanned row asks the router for the result file; when it is gone,
`rescanInOrigin` hands the target's name to that list and stays there, rather
than opening a security view on nothing. `workspaces.ScanRequestMsg` and
`ociresources.ScanRequestMsg` were **declared and unhandled** before this — dead
types carrying exactly the right shape — and they have handlers now.
`LaunchBatchScanMsg`, `LaunchSingleImageScanMsg` and `handleLaunchScan` went with
the form: they carried the options it had collected, and options come from the
configuration view.

**Coverage.** The deleted tests were covering live code incidentally, and two
regressions had to be repaired rather than accepted: the explorer's borrow
(`handleDirectorySelected`, `leaveSelectionMode`, `returnToOrigin` all fell to
0 %, exercised only by the security selection tests that went) and
`openSecurityView` (the two result handlers' success path). Both have their own
tests now, as do the two `ScanRequestMsg` handlers, `Init`, `handleSpinnerTick`
and the details viewport's scrolling. `internal/ui/security` 86.5 % → 87.2 %,
`internal/app` unchanged at 87.0 %, **no package lower than before**; project
total 81.5 % → 81.4 %, the residue of deleting a well-covered package's code.

`internal/ui/security/scan_test.go` was deleted whole. Its two durable
invariants live elsewhere: `ValidateTrivyServer` refusing `":"` is
`internal/scan/command_test.go`, and `alt+:` reaching the router rather than a
text field is `internal/app/command_mode_test.go`.

content.text:
Phase 3 faite et poussée sur la [PR #44](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/44). **2 538 lignes supprimées contre 530 ajoutées**, 32 fichiers.

Les deux prérequis du plan avaient bien atterri : `applyServerModeConstraints` dans la vue configuration, `ValidateTrivyServer` sur son champ `trivy_server`.

## Ce que le plan n'avait pas anticipé

**`StateScanning` est parti avec `StateInput`.** `startScan` avait deux appelants — le formulaire et le repli image du routeur — et une fois les deux disparus, toute la machinerie de scan en place n'avait plus d'utilisateur : canal de progression, `scanGen`, `cancelScan`, `waitForProgressCmd`, `purgeScanCacheCmd`, et trois messages. L'inventaire rescanne en arrière-plan avec un spinner sur la ligne, donc plus rien n'attend un écran entier pour une cible. `scan.go` s'est vidé sauf `hasScanSource`, déplacée près de son dernier appelant.

**Le pont de sélection est parti des deux côtés.** L'explorateur est le seul emprunteur restant, et seule la vue workspaces est prêtée — d'où la disparition de `NewForSelection`, `ImageSelectedMsg`, `ResetSelectionMsg` et `selectionMode` côté images.

## Le repli sur résultat manquant

Il ouvrait le formulaire avec la cible pré-remplie. Il reste maintenant dans la liste d'où vient la ligne et lui demande de rescanner. `workspaces.ScanRequestMsg` et `ociresources.ScanRequestMsg` étaient **déclarés sans handler** — des types morts portant exactement la bonne forme ; ils en ont un.

## Deux régressions de couverture réparées, pas acceptées

Les tests supprimés couvraient incidemment du code toujours vivant :

- **L'emprunt de l'explorateur** — `handleDirectorySelected`, `leaveSelectionMode` et `returnToOrigin` sont tombés à 0 %, exercés uniquement par les tests de sélection du formulaire.
- **`openSecurityView`** — le chemin nominal des deux handlers de résultat.

Les deux ont leurs propres tests désormais, comme les deux handlers `ScanRequestMsg`, `Init`, `handleSpinnerTick` et le défilement du panneau de détails.

`internal/ui/security` 86.5 % → **87.2 %**, `internal/app` inchangé à 87.0 %, **aucun paquet en baisse**. Total projet 81.5 % → 81.4 % : le résidu arithmétique de supprimer du code mieux couvert que la moyenne, pas une régression — je l'ai vérifié paquet par paquet contre `HEAD`.

`scan_test.go` supprimé en entier ; ses deux invariants durables vivent ailleurs (`ValidateTrivyServer` refusant `":"` dans `internal/scan`, `alt+:` dans `internal/app`).

## Reste à faire

La suppression du SBOM (§3.14) est maintenant débloquée — c'était l'attente. J'ai mis l'entrée à jour : la renumérotation qui la rendait risquée n'a plus lieu d'être, il ne reste que la liste de `internal/config` vers le bas.

Toujours pas lancé le TUI : les vérifications manuelles de la PR restent à cocher, et j'ajouterais maintenant « `enter` sur une ligne dont le fichier de résultat a disparu » aux deux listes.

59	## Git workflow — pull requests only
60	
61	**Never push directly to `main`.** The Entire mirror rejects it:
62	
63	```
64	! [remote rejected] main -> main (protected branch)
65	```
66	
67	This is enforced by the mirror, not by GitHub, and **Entire does not document it**
68	— neither the CLI help nor `docs.entire.io` mentions a protected default branch.
69	The only branch restriction Entire states is that `entire/unmirrored/*` is never
70	forwarded. Treat the rejection as observed behaviour, not as a specified one.
71	
72	What rules GitHub out is that branch protection is *unavailable* on this
73	repository: it is private on a free personal plan, so both endpoints answer
74	`403 Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public` —
75	`/repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main/protection` and `/repos/anthnel/devdesk/rulesets`
76	alike. Do not cite `gh api repos/anthnel/devdesk/branches/main` reporting
77	`"protected": false` as the proof: that field only ever reflects legacy branch
78	protection, so it reads `false` under a ruleset too, and on this plan it would
79	read `false` whatever the configuration. The 403 is the evidence; the `false` is
80	not.
81	
82	Every other branch, including `entire/checkpoints/v1`, pushes through the mirror
83	and is forwarded to GitHub.
84	
85	**Pull requests are GitHub's, not Entire's.** Entire has no merge-request
86	concept — it layers checkpoints and sessions over git and forwards pushes. So
87	the PR steps below are `gh`, and the branch they review is one `origin` carried
88	to GitHub. `entire review` (labs) runs a multi-agent review against the current
89	branch and is a pre-merge step, not a substitute for the PR.
90	
91	```bash
92	git switch -c <branch>                          # work
93	git push origin <branch>                        # via the mirror — forwarded to GitHub
94	gh pr create -R anthnel/devdesk --base main --head <branch>
95	gh pr merge -R anthnel/devdesk <n> --squash --delete-branch
96	git fetch origin main && git merge --ff-only origin/main   # may need a retry, see below
97	```
98	
99	**`-R anthnel/devdesk` is not optional.** `gh` infers the repository from a
100	remote pointing at a GitHub host, and `origin` is an `entire://` URL, so it
101	finds none and fails with *"none of the git remotes configured for this
102	repository point to a known GitHub host"*. The flag names the repo directly.
103	Do not solve this by adding a GitHub remote — see below.
104	
105	**After a merge, `origin` can read stale for a minute or two.** The mirror lags
106	GitHub, so `git fetch origin` right after `gh pr merge` may return the *previous*
107	`main` — with no error, which is the part that misleads. `gh pr view <n> --json state`
108	says `MERGED` while `git rev-parse origin/main` still points at the commit before
109	it. Re-run the fetch a moment later; `gh` is what to trust in the meantime,
110	because it talks to GitHub directly and needs no remote.
111	
112	**Do not add a second remote pointing at GitHub to work around that.** It would
113	be the one path that defeats the only protection there is: `main` cannot be
114	protected on GitHub here (see the 403 above), so the mirror's refusal is the
115	whole of it, and `git push github main` would simply succeed. A direct push also
116	bypasses the mirror, and with it the Entire hook that records checkpoints and
117	sessions — which is not visible until much later. `origin` is the only remote,
118	deliberately.
119	
120	**Merging several branches cut from the same commit conflicts in
121	`docs/backlog.md`.** Every fix inserts its entry at the top of §1.1, so the
122	second and third merges land on the same anchor. The resolution is always to
123	keep both sides — they are independent entries, not competing edits.
124	
125	### Remotes
126	
127	| Remote | URL | Use |
128	|--------|-----|-----|
129	| `origin` | `entire://aws-eu-central-1.entire.io/gh/anthnel/devdesk` | Entire mirror — everything: clone, fetch, push |
130	
131	**There is one remote, and there should stay one.** The repository is hosted on
132	GitHub and mirrored to EntireDB in `aws-eu-central-1` (a second placement exists
133	in `aws-us-east-2`), but every git operation goes through the mirror: it is the
134	regional path, it is what keeps agent reads fast, and it is where the checkpoint
135	hook runs. Anything needing GitHub's own answer — PR state, review threads —
136	goes through `gh`, which authenticates directly and does not need a remote.
137	
138	Semantic search (`entire search`, and the `entire:*` skills that depend on it) is
139	**not available in the EU region** — the server answers `semantic search is not
140	yet available in the region(s) hosting this search`. Nothing in the repo config
141	fixes this.
142

`main` avait avancé de deux commits pendant le travail, dont **[#46 qui change la doctrine git du projet](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/46)** : il n'y a plus qu'un seul remote (`origin`), `gh` exige `-R anthnel/devdesk`, et le fast-forward post-merge se fait depuis `origin`, pas depuis un remote GitHub.

J'ai donc fusionné `main` dans la branche avant de merger, plutôt que de fusionner à l'aveugle. `CLAUDE.md` s'est auto-résolu sans conflit — leur réécriture du workflow git et mes sections vue security touchent des parties disjointes — et j'ai vérifié que les deux côtés survivaient avant de committer. Build, vet, lint et suite complète repassés après la fusion, puis à nouveau sur `main`.

**À signaler** : ton checkout local a encore un remote `github`, que #46 dit explicitement de ne pas garder — l'argument est qu'un push direct contournerait à la fois le refus du miroir sur `main` (la seule protection existante, la protection GitHub étant indisponible sur ce plan) et le hook Entire qui enregistre checkpoints et sessions. Je l'ai utilisé en lecture seule au début de cette session, avant de lire #46. Je ne l'ai pas supprimé : c'est une modification de ta config locale que tu n'as pas demandée. `git remote remove github` si tu veux t'aligner.

## Reste ouvert

§3.14, la suppression du SBOM, maintenant débloquée — la renumérotation du formulaire qui la rendait risquée n'existe plus. Et les vérifications manuelles du TUI que je n'ai toujours pas faites.

skills.content:
# Plan Command

This command creates a comprehensive implementation plan before writing any code. It accepts either free-form requirements or a PRD markdown file.

Run inline by default. Do not call the Task tool or any subagent by default. This keeps `/plan` usable from plugin installs that ship commands without agent files.

## What This Command Does

1. **Restate Requirements** - Clarify what needs to be built
2. **Identify Risks** - Surface potential issues and blockers
3. **Create Step Plan** - Break down implementation into phases
4. **Wait for Confirmation** - MUST receive user approval before proceeding

## When to Use

Use `/plan` when:
- Starting a new feature
- Making significant architectural changes
- Working on complex refactoring
- Multiple files/components will be affected
- Requirements are unclear or ambiguous

## How It Works

The assistant will:

1. **Analyze the request** and restate requirements in clear terms
2. **Ground the plan** in relevant codebase patterns when the repo is available
3. **Break down into phases** with specific, actionable steps
4. **Identify dependencies** between components
5. **Assess risks** and potential blockers
6. **Estimate complexity** (High/Medium/Low)
7. **Present the plan** and WAIT for your explicit confirmation

## Input Modes

| Input | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path/to/name.prd.md` | PRD artifact mode | Read the PRD, pick the next pending delivery milestone or implementation phase, and write `.claude/plans/{name}.plan.md` |
| Any other markdown path | Reference mode | Read the file as context and produce an inline plan |
| Free-form text | Conversational mode | Produce an inline plan |
| Empty input | Clarification mode | Ask what should be planned |

In PRD artifact mode, create `.claude/plans/` if needed. If the PRD contains a `Delivery Milestones` table, update only the selected row from `pending` to `in-progress` and set its `Plan` cell to the generated plan path. If the PRD uses the legacy `.claude/PRPs/prds/` format with `Implementation Phases`, read it without migrating paths.

## Pattern Grounding

Before writing the plan, search the codebase for conventions the implementation should mirror. Capture the top example for each relevant category with file references:

| Category | What to capture |
|---|---|
| Naming | File, function, type, command, or script naming in the affected area |
| Error handling | How failures are raised, returned, logged, or handled gracefully |
| Logging | Levels, format, and what gets logged |
| Data access | Repository, service, query, or filesystem patterns |
| Tests | Test file location, framework, fixtures, and assertion style |

If no similar code exists, state that explicitly. Do not invent a pattern.

## PRD Artifact Output

When called with a `.prd.md` file, write the plan to `.claude/plans/{kebab-case-name}.plan.md` using this structure:

````markdown
# Plan: {Feature Name}

**Source PRD**: {path}
**Selected Milestone**: {milestone or phase name}
**Complexity**: {Small | Medium | Large}

## Summary
{2-3 sentences}

## Patterns to Mirror
| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Errors | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Tests | `path:line` | {short description} |

## Files to Change
| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE | {reason} |

## Tasks
### Task 1: {name}
- **Action**: {what to do}
- **Mirror**: {pattern to follow}
- **Validate**: {command that proves correctness}

## Validation
```bash
{project-specific validation commands}
```

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

## Acceptance
- [ ] All tasks complete
- [ ] Validation passes
- [ ] Patterns mirrored, not reinvented
````

After writing the artifact, report its path and WAIT for confirmation before writing code.

## Example Usage

```
User: /plan I need to add real-time notifications when markets resolve

Assistant:
# Implementation Plan: Real-Time Market Resolution Notifications

## Requirements Restatement
- Send notifications to users when markets they're watching resolve
- Support multiple notification channels (in-app, email, webhook)
- Ensure notifications are delivered reliably
- Include market outcome and user's position result

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Database Schema
- Add notifications table with columns: id, user_id, market_id, type, status, created_at
- Add user_notification_preferences table for channel preferences
- Create indexes on user_id and market_id for performance

### Phase 2: Notification Service
- Create notification service in lib/notifications.ts
- Implement notification queue using BullMQ/Redis
- Add retry logic for failed deliveries
- Create notification templates

### Phase 3: Integration Points
- Hook into market resolution logic (when status changes to "resolved")
- Query all users with positions in market
- Enqueue notifications for each user

### Phase 4: Frontend Components
- Create NotificationBell component in header
- Add NotificationList modal
- Implement real-time updates via Supabase subscriptions
- Add notification preferences page

## Dependencies
- Redis (for queue)
- Email service (SendGrid/Resend)
- Supabase real-time subscriptions

## Risks
- HIGH: Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM required)
- MEDIUM: Performance with 1000+ users per market
- MEDIUM: Notification spam if markets resolve frequently
- LOW: Real-time subscription overhead

## Estimated Complexity: MEDIUM
- Backend: 4-6 hours
- Frontend: 3-4 hours
- Testing: 2-3 hours
- Total: 9-13 hours

**WAITING FOR CONFIRMATION**: Proceed with this plan? (yes/no/modify)
```

## Important Notes

**CRITICAL**: This command will **NOT** write any code until you explicitly confirm the plan with "yes" or "proceed" or similar affirmative response.

If you want changes, respond with:
- "modify: [your changes]"
- "different approach: [alternative]"
- "skip phase 2 and do phase 3 first"

## Integration with Other Commands

After planning:
- Use the `tdd-workflow` skill to implement with test-driven development
- Use `/build-fix` if build errors occur
- Use `/code-review` to review completed implementation
- Use `/pr` or `/prp-pr` to open a pull request

> **Need requirements first?** Use `/plan-prd` for a lean PRD at `.claude/prds/{name}.prd.md`.
>
> **Need the legacy PRP flow?** Use `/prp-plan` for deep PRP planning with `.claude/PRPs/` artifacts. Use `/prp-implement` to execute those plans with rigorous validation loops.

## Optional Planner Agent

ECC also provides a `planner` agent for manual installs that include agent files. Use it only when the local runtime already exposes that subagent and the user explicitly asks you to delegate planning.

If the `planner` subagent is unavailable, continue planning inline instead of surfacing an "Agent type 'planner' not found" error.

For manual installs, the source file lives at:
`agents/planner.md`

`GetHelpContent` "Scan Types" section carried an `SBOM Generation:` line. The
survey listed the help text under "two strings to reword" but named only
`fields.go`; this one is a deletion, not a rewording.

single builder.** It asserted that `trivyMisconfigArgs` and `sbomArgs` both
refuse `":"`, and the second was being deleted. `trivySecretArgs` also takes a
server address and was covered by nothing, so it took the SBOM line's place —
the test now means what its name says again rather than shrinking to one case.

[]SBOMComponent` and `SBOMComponent` exist nowhere. Checking the rest of the
same block, neither do `Vulnerability`, `Secret`, `Misconfig` or `License`: the
real `Result` carries one flat `Findings []Finding`, and which family a finding

```go
  FixCommand  string
}
```

`trivy-secret` rather than being recognised by the presence of `Match`.
`Fingerprint` is Gitleaks-only, and it is why `i` (add to `.gitleaksignore`) is
offered for Gitleaks findings alone.

type SeverityLevel string"""

SBOM generation is gone. [PR #47](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/47) — 22 files, +127/−397.

## What went

The two settings, their two controls in `:config`, the scan stage, `Result.SBOMPath`, and five functions (`GetSBOMCommand`, `GenerateSBOM`, `sbomArgs`, `sbomSubcommand`, `sbomFileName`) plus the `containerOutputPath` constant. `dockerSocketMount` stays — `wrapTrivy` uses it too, and deleting both together was the trap the survey flagged.

Build, vet, lint (0 issues) and the full suite are green.

## Three things the survey didn't have right

**It missed a file.** `internal/ui/security/header.go` had an `SBOM Generation:` line in the help text. The survey listed help text as "strings to reword" but named only `fields.go`.

**A test would have quietly shrunk.** `TestEveryTrivyBuilderRefusesAnUnusableServer` checked that the misconfig *and* SBOM builders refuse a malformed address. Deleting half would leave a test named "every builder" checking one. `trivySecretArgs` also takes an address and was covered by nothing — so it took the vacant slot.

**The codemaps were fiction, not stale.** The survey noted `SBOMComponent` exists nowhere. Checking the rest of that block, neither do `Vulnerability`, `Secret`, `Misconfig` or `License` — the real `Result` carries one flat `Findings []Finding`. Removing only the SBOM lines would have left four invented types looking freshly reviewed, so I replaced the block with what the code declares.

## A claim I had to retract

Survey point 6 said `TestEveryConfiguredOptionReachesTheScanner` "fails if only one side is done." I probed it: **it does not.** The test walks fields the two structs *share*, so a field in one and not the other is never visited. What it actually catches is a field left in both and unwired — confirmed by making it fail. The half-done state was covered by the compiler all along, so the removal was still safe, but the backlog now says the true thing.

I also promoted point 2 from a manual check to a test: `TestAConfigCarryingTheRetiredSBOMKeysStillLoads` fails the day someone adds `KnownFields(true)` to the loader.

## Two caveats

`mise run test-race` **did not run** — no `gcc` on PATH, as `CLAUDE.md` documents. This change removes a goroutine rather than adding one, so the risk is low, but it's untested.

Coverage: `internal/ui/configuration` 83.4% → 83.2% and total 81.4% → 81.3%. Not a regression — a function-by-function diff shows every percentage identical; it's the arithmetic of deleting a covered line.

The TUI still wants a manual look at the `scan` tab and a scan from `:sec` before merge.
