## Ce qui est fait

`cloneSelection` : appartenance par **ancêtre marqué le plus proche**. Une racine inclut tout ce qui est dessous, une exclusion coupe un sous-arbre, et une racine sous une exclusion rallume la branche à n'importe quelle profondeur. Le tri-état se calcule sans aucun appel réseau.

Le test qui mérite d'exister : `acme/platform-tools` n'est **pas** un enfant de `acme/platform`. Sans le séparateur final, la comparaison par préfixe l'aurait inclus — et personne ne l'aurait vu avant de cloner un dépôt de trop.

La suite est la partie lourde, et elle se découpe en trois blocs dont **un est un refactor à risque** :

1. **`explorerRow`** — la décision 14 impose un type de ligne, donc la table passe de `Model[*TreeNode]` à `Model[explorerRow]`. Ça touche toutes les colonnes, `Selected()`, et chaque handler qui résout le curseur. C'est mécanique mais transverse.
2. **Le mode sélection** — colonne de case, `Space`, en-tête avec les compteurs, raccourcis, aide.
3. **Le pipeline découverte/clone** — messages, concurrence bornée par `ParallelJobs`, annulation à deux portées.

Ma session est longue et le bloc 1 est exactement le type de changement que les règles du projet déconseillent d'entamer en fin de contexte : transverse, multi-fichiers, et cassant tant qu'il n'est pas terminé. Un arbre qui ne compile pas serait un plus mauvais point d'arrêt que celui-ci.

Everything the explorer pull rework needs before the rework itself: the design,
two dead settings removed, two defects fixed, and the selection model. **No
user-visible behaviour changes except the two defects** — the new mode is not
started.

## The design (§3.16, §3.17)

Fourteen settled decisions, out of a brainstorm. The one the rest hangs on:

> **The explorer creates what does not exist, workspaces reconciles what does.**

So the explorer *clones* and skips what is on disk, and every question about a
dirty working copy moves to a `sync` feature in the workspaces view (§3.17) —
which turns out to be mostly data `workspaces.Entry` already computes. That
single line collapsed the per-row states from nine to five and settled the
naming: it was never the behaviour that was wrong, only the label.

Two more worth calling out:

**Discovery and cloning are pipelined**, not list-then-clone. A complete list
first means walking the whole tree through the API before anything happens,
which moves the freeze one screen earlier rather than removing it. Accepted
cost: the total is only known at the end.

**The on-disk tree mirrors the forge root.** `nodeSlug` keeps only the last path
segment today, so with several groups selected `acme/platform` and
`other/platform` would both land on `~/ws/platform` and merge silently.

## Two defects fixed

**D34 — nothing paginated.** Every list in `explorer/api.go` was
`PerPage: 100, Page: 1`, at five sites, so a group with more than 100 subgroups
or projects was silently truncated: the explorer showed fewer children than it
had and a recursive clone skipped repositories without saying so. `listAll`
walks every page and the four calls go through it — one loop, because four
copies is how one ends up wrong.

It stops on `NextPage <= Page` rather than `NextPage == 0` alone: that also
catches a server pointing back at the page just served, and unlike a page cap it
is a bound that cannot cut a legitimate response short. A cap would be the very
defect being fixed, wearing a different hat.

**Discovery decorated what a clone never reads.** The recursive walk paid two
requests per project for a pipeline status and an access level — 400+ calls on
two hundred repositories for a CI badge and a role. `listGroupChildren` is now
the undecorated half both callers share; `discoverGroupChildren` decorates
nothing, `loadChildren` decorates as before.

That made the two kinds of node non-interchangeable, so the clone also stopped
storing what it finds on `node.Children` — discovery nodes on the tree the view
renders would blank the role and CI columns for every group a clone walked
through. **That write was also the Rule 110 race**, so it goes with it. The
backlog had it recorded as something the rework would remove by construction;
the lighter fetch made keeping it actively harmful, which brought it forward.

## Two settings deleted

Both were declared, defaulted, editable in `:config` — and read by nobody.

`gitlab.pull.target_dir` duplicated `app.workspaces_dir`, with defaults
differing by a single letter (`~/workspace` against `~/workspaces`), so setting
the wrong one changed nothing and said nothing.

`gitlab.pull.max_depth` is the more interesting one: it is not merely unread, it
**contradicts decision 10**. Tick a group, have discovery stop at level five,
and you get less than you asked for with nothing saying so — the silent
truncation of D34, reintroduced as a feature. Exclusions express the same intent
precisely. Deleting it also removes a name clash: §3.6 settles a *different*
`MaxDepth`, the depth a forge declares.

`TestAConfigCarryingTheRetiredSBOMKeysStillLoads` was generalised into
`TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` rather than copied twice — what it
pins is `Load`'s tolerance of retired keys, not any one setting.

## The selection model

`cloneSelection` is roots plus exclusions. Membership is the nearest marked
ancestor-or-self, so a root includes everything below it, an exclusion cuts a
subtree, and a root under an exclusion turns that branch back on at any depth.

It answers everything the UI needs **without discovering anything**, which is
the reason for the shape rather than a bonus: a positive list of repositories
cannot be built without enumerating a group the moment it is ticked. A group
nobody has expanded is still selectable and still shows a correct tri-state.

Ten tests, every one naming a node that was never fetched. The one that earns
its place: `acme/platform-tools` must not be a child of `acme/platform` —
without the trailing separator it is, and nobody would notice until a
repository too many had been cloned.

## Also recorded

**D35** — `GitUnpulled` comes from `rev-list HEAD..@{u}` and nothing ever runs
`git fetch`, so the column reads `0` on a repository forty commits behind. Not a
missing feature; a number that looks authoritative and is not. Blocks §3.17.

**D36** — `CachedGroups` / `CachedProjects` are cleared in three places and
never filled by any production code.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l .` clean
- [x] `mise run lint` — 0 issues
- [x] `go test ./...` — green
- [x] `go test -race` on the touched packages — green (mingw-w64 installed this
      session, so this ran locally for the first time)
- [x] The three pagination tests were run against the pre-fix code and **fail**
      on it
- [x] `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer` coverage 90.4%, unchanged
- [ ] Manual: browse a group with more than 100 projects, and check the role and
      CI columns are still populated after a recursive pull

## What is not in this

The rework itself: the `explorerRow` row type, the selection mode, and the
discovery/clone pipeline. The design is complete and both prerequisites are
cleared, so those are next.
BODY

Mergée. `main` est sur `7fab711`, arbre propre.

Les branches `entire/*` sont intactes — c'était le point à vérifier avant de purger, et le prune n'a retiré que des refs de suivi dont la contrepartie distante n'existait plus (12 branches de feature déjà mergées).

## Bilan de la session

Quatre PR mergées :

| PR | Contenu |
|---|---|
| #47 | Retrait du SBOM, plus un test bancal réparé |
| #48 | Conception §3.16/§3.17, suppression de `target_dir`, D34–D36 |
| #49 | Pagination, découverte allégée, modèle de sélection |

Plus l'outillage : le **détecteur de race fonctionne en local** (`scoop install mingw`), et le remote `github` a été retiré conformément à la doctrine du dépôt.

## Deux choses à retenir pour la suite

**`gh pr merge --auto` ne fait pas ce qu'il annonce ici.** L'auto-merge n'est pas disponible sur ce dépôt, et `gh` retombe silencieusement sur un merge immédiat. Sur #48 j'ai fusionné pendant que la CI tournait encore. Il faut attendre les checks, puis merger.

**`mise run test-race` demande un terminal neuf** — le processus courant a hérité du PATH d'avant l'installation de mingw.

## Ce qui reste

La vérification manuelle de #49 : un groupe de plus de 100 projets, et les colonnes rôle et CI après un pull récursif.

Puis le rework lui-même, dans l'ordre : `explorerRow` (le refactor transverse), le mode sélection, le pipeline découverte/clone. La conception est complète et les deux préalables sont levés — il ne reste que de l'exécution.

skills.content:
# Plan Command

This command creates a comprehensive implementation plan before writing any code. It accepts either free-form requirements or a PRD markdown file.

Run inline by default. Do not call the Task tool or any subagent by default. This keeps `/plan` usable from plugin installs that ship commands without agent files.

## What This Command Does

1. **Restate Requirements** - Clarify what needs to be built
2. **Identify Risks** - Surface potential issues and blockers
3. **Create Step Plan** - Break down implementation into phases
4. **Wait for Confirmation** - MUST receive user approval before proceeding

## When to Use

Use `/plan` when:
- Starting a new feature
- Making significant architectural changes
- Working on complex refactoring
- Multiple files/components will be affected
- Requirements are unclear or ambiguous

## How It Works

The assistant will:

1. **Analyze the request** and restate requirements in clear terms
2. **Ground the plan** in relevant codebase patterns when the repo is available
3. **Break down into phases** with specific, actionable steps
4. **Identify dependencies** between components
5. **Assess risks** and potential blockers
6. **Estimate complexity** (High/Medium/Low)
7. **Present the plan** and WAIT for your explicit confirmation

## Input Modes

| Input | Mode | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `path/to/name.prd.md` | PRD artifact mode | Read the PRD, pick the next pending delivery milestone or implementation phase, and write `.claude/plans/{name}.plan.md` |
| Any other markdown path | Reference mode | Read the file as context and produce an inline plan |
| Free-form text | Conversational mode | Produce an inline plan |
| Empty input | Clarification mode | Ask what should be planned |

In PRD artifact mode, create `.claude/plans/` if needed. If the PRD contains a `Delivery Milestones` table, update only the selected row from `pending` to `in-progress` and set its `Plan` cell to the generated plan path. If the PRD uses the legacy `.claude/PRPs/prds/` format with `Implementation Phases`, read it without migrating paths.

## Pattern Grounding

Before writing the plan, search the codebase for conventions the implementation should mirror. Capture the top example for each relevant category with file references:

| Category | What to capture |
|---|---|
| Naming | File, function, type, command, or script naming in the affected area |
| Error handling | How failures are raised, returned, logged, or handled gracefully |
| Logging | Levels, format, and what gets logged |
| Data access | Repository, service, query, or filesystem patterns |
| Tests | Test file location, framework, fixtures, and assertion style |

If no similar code exists, state that explicitly. Do not invent a pattern.

## PRD Artifact Output

When called with a `.prd.md` file, write the plan to `.claude/plans/{kebab-case-name}.plan.md` using this structure:

````markdown
# Plan: {Feature Name}

**Source PRD**: {path}
**Selected Milestone**: {milestone or phase name}
**Complexity**: {Small | Medium | Large}

## Summary
{2-3 sentences}

## Patterns to Mirror
| Category | Source | Pattern |
|---|---|---|
| Naming | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Errors | `path:line` | {short description} |
| Tests | `path:line` | {short description} |

## Files to Change
| File | Action | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE | {reason} |

## Tasks
### Task 1: {name}
- **Action**: {what to do}
- **Mirror**: {pattern to follow}
- **Validate**: {command that proves correctness}

## Validation
```bash
{project-specific validation commands}
```

## Risks
| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

## Acceptance
- [ ] All tasks complete
- [ ] Validation passes
- [ ] Patterns mirrored, not reinvented
````

After writing the artifact, report its path and WAIT for confirmation before writing code.

## Example Usage

```
User: /plan I need to add real-time notifications when markets resolve

Assistant:
# Implementation Plan: Real-Time Market Resolution Notifications

## Requirements Restatement
- Send notifications to users when markets they're watching resolve
- Support multiple notification channels (in-app, email, webhook)
- Ensure notifications are delivered reliably
- Include market outcome and user's position result

## Implementation Phases

### Phase 1: Database Schema
- Add notifications table with columns: id, user_id, market_id, type, status, created_at
- Add user_notification_preferences table for channel preferences
- Create indexes on user_id and market_id for performance

### Phase 2: Notification Service
- Create notification service in lib/notifications.ts
- Implement notification queue using BullMQ/Redis
- Add retry logic for failed deliveries
- Create notification templates

### Phase 3: Integration Points
- Hook into market resolution logic (when status changes to "resolved")
- Query all users with positions in market
- Enqueue notifications for each user

### Phase 4: Frontend Components
- Create NotificationBell component in header
- Add NotificationList modal
- Implement real-time updates via Supabase subscriptions
- Add notification preferences page

## Dependencies
- Redis (for queue)
- Email service (SendGrid/Resend)
- Supabase real-time subscriptions

## Risks
- HIGH: Email deliverability (SPF/DKIM required)
- MEDIUM: Performance with 1000+ users per market
- MEDIUM: Notification spam if markets resolve frequently
- LOW: Real-time subscription overhead

## Estimated Complexity: MEDIUM
- Backend: 4-6 hours
- Frontend: 3-4 hours
- Testing: 2-3 hours
- Total: 9-13 hours

**WAITING FOR CONFIRMATION**: Proceed with this plan? (yes/no/modify)
```

## Important Notes

**CRITICAL**: This command will **NOT** write any code until you explicitly confirm the plan with "yes" or "proceed" or similar affirmative response.

If you want changes, respond with:
- "modify: [your changes]"
- "different approach: [alternative]"
- "skip phase 2 and do phase 3 first"

## Integration with Other Commands

After planning:
- Use the `tdd-workflow` skill to implement with test-driven development
- Use `/build-fix` if build errors occur
- Use `/code-review` to review completed implementation
- Use `/pr` or `/prp-pr` to open a pull request

> **Need requirements first?** Use `/plan-prd` for a lean PRD at `.claude/prds/{name}.prd.md`.
>
> **Need the legacy PRP flow?** Use `/prp-plan` for deep PRP planning with `.claude/PRPs/` artifacts. Use `/prp-implement` to execute those plans with rigorous validation loops.

## Optional Planner Agent

ECC also provides a `planner` agent for manual installs that include agent files. Use it only when the local runtime already exposes that subagent and the user explicitly asks you to delegate planning.

If the `planner` subagent is unavailable, continue planning inline instead of surfacing an "Agent type 'planner' not found" error.

For manual installs, the source file lives at:
`agents/planner.md`

80	// timeBefore compares two nullable times (nil is considered "oldest")
81	func timeBefore(a, b *time.Time) bool {
82		if a == nil && b == nil {
83			return false
84		}
85		if a == nil {

7	
8	// NodeType représente le type de nœud dans l'arbre
9	type NodeType string
10	
11	const (
12		NodeTypeGroup   NodeType = "group"
13		NodeTypeProject NodeType = "project"
14	)
15	
16	// TreeNode représente un nœud dans l'arbre GitLab
17	type TreeNode struct {
18		ID       int64 // GitLab uses int64 for IDs
19		Name     string
20		FullPath string
21		Type     NodeType
22		Children []*TreeNode
23		Expanded bool
24		Loading  bool // True when loading children
25		Parent   *TreeNode
26		Depth    int // Depth in tree (for rendering)
27	
28		// Metadata for flat table display
29		Visibility        string     // "private", "internal", "public"
30		AccessLevel       int        // User's access level (0=none, 10=guest, 20=reporter, 30=dev, 40=maintainer, 50=owner)
31		CreatedAt         *time.Time // Creation date
32		LastActivityAt    *time.Time // Last activity date
33		PipelineStatus    string     // Last pipeline status ("success", "failed", "running", "pending", etc.)
34		MarkedForDeletion bool       // True if the project is already scheduled for deletion
35		WebURL            string     // Full HTTPS URL for opening in browser
36	}
37	
38	// IsExpandable retourne vrai si le nœud peut être étendu
39	func (n *TreeNode) IsExpandable() bool {
40		return n.Type == NodeTypeGroup
41	}
42	
43	// Toggle expande ou contracte le nœud
44	func (n *TreeNode) Toggle() {
45		if n.IsExpandable() {
46			n.Expanded = !n.Expanded
47		}
48	}
49	
50	// AccessLevelName returns a human-readable role name for the access level
51	func (n *TreeNode) AccessLevelName() string {
52		switch {
53		case n.AccessLevel >= 50:
54			return "Owner"
55		case n.AccessLevel >= 40:
56			return "Maintainer"
57		case n.AccessLevel >= 30:
58			return "Developer"
59		case n.AccessLevel >= 20:
60			return "Reporter"
61		case n.AccessLevel >= 10:
62			return "Guest"
63		default:
64			return ""
65		}
66	}
67	
68	// nodeSlug returns the last path segment of a GitLab FullPath (the URL slug)
69	func nodeSlug(fullPath string) string {
70		parts := strings.Split(fullPath, "/")
71		return parts[len(parts)-1]
72	}

14	// Update gère les messages
15	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
16		switch msg := msg.(type) {
17		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
18			m.width = msg.Width
19			m.height = msg.Height
20			m.resize(msg.Width, msg.Height)
21	
22		case tea.KeyMsg:
23			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
24	
25		case spinner.TickMsg:
26			if m.loading {
27				var cmd tea.Cmd
28				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
29				return m, cmd
30			}
31	
32		case RootGroupsLoadedMsg:
33			m.loading = false
34			m.firstLoadDone = true
35			m.nodes = msg.Nodes
36			m.error = ""
37			m.updateTableRows()
38			m.table.GotoTop()
39			// If there's a pending selection, expand path to it
40			if m.pendingSelectPath != "" {
41				return m.expandToPath(m.pendingSelectPath)
42			}
43	
44		case ChildrenLoadedMsg:
45			return m.handleChildrenLoaded(msg)
46	
47		case LoadErrorMsg:
48			return m.handleLoadError(msg)
49	
50		case PullDestinationSelectedMsg:
51			return m.handlePullDestinationSelected(msg)
52	
53		case PullSelectionCancelledMsg:
54			m.pullTargetNode = nil
55			return m, nil
56	
57		case PullCompleteMsg:
58			return m.handlePullComplete(msg)
59	
60		case components.ReportModalCloseMsg:
61			m.mode = ModeNormal
62			m.reportModal = nil
63			return m, nil
64	
65		case components.CreationFormSubmitMsg:
66			return m.handleCreationSubmit(msg)
67	
68		case components.CreationFormCancelMsg:
69			m.mode = ModeNormal
70			m.creationForm = nil
71			return m, nil
72	
73		case TemplatesLoadedMsg:
74			return m.handleTemplatesLoaded(msg)
75	
76		case GroupCreatedMsg:
77			return m.handleGroupCreated(msg)
78	
79		case ProjectCreatedMsg:
80			return m.handleProjectCreated(msg)
81	
82		case components.DeleteConfirmModalYesMsg:
83			return m.handleDeleteConfirmed(msg.PermanentlyRemove)
84	
85		case components.DeleteConfirmModalNoMsg:
86			m.mode = ModeNormal
87			m.deleteConfirmModal = nil
88			m.deleteTargetNode = nil
89			return m, nil

93

95			if msg.Error != nil {
96				log.Printf("ERROR [explorer] open browser: %v", msg.Error)
97				m.footerError = "Failed to open browser — check logs"

112	// handleKeyMsg handles keyboard input
113	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
114		// Filter bar search mode - prioritaire
115		if m.table.InEditMode() {
116			return m, m.table.Update(msg)
117		}
118	
119		// Handle mode-specific input
120		switch m.mode {
121		case ModeShowingReport:
122			if m.reportModal != nil {
123				var cmd tea.Cmd
124				m.reportModal, cmd = m.reportModal.Update(msg)
125				return m, cmd
126			}
127		case ModePulling, ModeLoadingTemplates:
128			// Ignore input while pulling or loading templates
129			return m, nil
130		case ModeCreatingProject:
131			if m.creationForm != nil {
132				var cmd tea.Cmd

134				return m, cmd
135			}
136		case ModeConfirmingDelete:
137			if m.deleteConfirmModal != nil {
138				var cmd tea.Cmd
139				m.deleteConfirmModal, cmd = m.deleteConfirmModal.Update(msg)
140				return m, cmd
141			}
142		}
143	
144		// Normal mode. Actions resolve the cursor through the table, which resolves
145		// it against the very slice its rows were built from.
146		switch msg.String() {
147		case "left", "h":
148			return m.handleDrillUp()
149		case "right", "l":
150			return m.handleDrillDown()
151		case "esc":
152			return m.handleDrillUp()
153		case "ctrl+r":
154			return m.handleRefresh()
155		case "p":
156			return m.handlePullStart()
157		case "ctrl+n":
158			return m.handleCreateResource()
159		case "ctrl+d":
160			return m.handleDeleteStart()
161		case "ctrl+w":
162			return m.handleOpenInBrowser()
163		}
164	
165		// Navigation, `/` and `.` are the table's, not the view's.
166		return m, m.table.Update(msg)
167	}

169	// handleOpenInBrowser opens the selected node's web URL in the default browser
170	func (m Model) handleOpenInBrowser() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
171		node, ok := m.table.Selected()
172		if !ok || node.WebURL == "" {
173			return m, nil
174		}
175		url := node.WebURL
176		return m, func() tea.Msg {
177			var cmd *exec.Cmd
178			switch runtime.GOOS {
179			case "darwin":

181			case "windows":
182				cmd = exec.Command("cmd", "/c", "start", url)
183			default:
184				cmd = exec.Command("xdg-open", url)
185			}
186			return BrowserOpenedMsg{Error: cmd.Start()}
187		}

3	import (
4		"strings"
5	
6		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
7	)
8	
9	// handleDrillDown handles enter key - navigate into a group
10	func (m Model) handleDrillDown() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
11		node, ok := m.table.Selected()
12		if !ok || node.Type != NodeTypeGroup {
13			return m, nil
14		}
15	
16		// Save cursor position before navigating down
17		m.cursorStack = append(m.cursorStack, m.table.Cursor())
18		// Push current group onto navigation stack
19		m.navigationStack = append(m.navigationStack, m.currentGroupNode)
20		m.currentGroupNode = node
21		m.activeTabIndex = m.tabCount() - 1
22	
23		// Load children if not yet loaded
24		if node.Children == nil {
25			node.Loading = true
26			m.loading = true
27			m.updateTableRows()
28			return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, m.loadChildren(node))
29		}
30		m.updateTableRows()
31		m.table.GotoTop()
32		return m, nil
33	}
34	
35	// handleDrillUp handles backspace key - navigate back to parent
36	func (m Model) handleDrillUp() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
37		if len(m.navigationStack) == 0 {
38			return m, nil
39		}
40		// Pop from stack
41		m.currentGroupNode = m.navigationStack[len(m.navigationStack)-1]
42		m.navigationStack = m.navigationStack[:len(m.navigationStack)-1]
43		m.activeTabIndex = m.tabCount() - 1
44		m.updateTableRows()
45		// Restore cursor position at the parent level
46		if len(m.cursorStack) > 0 {
47			cursor := m.cursorStack[len(m.cursorStack)-1]
48			m.cursorStack = m.cursorStack[:len(m.cursorStack)-1]
49			m.table.SetCursor(cursor)
50		} else {
51			m.table.GotoTop()
52		}
53		return m, nil
54	}
55	
56	// updateTableRows refills the table with the current drill-down level.
57	//
58	// The sort, the filter, the sort arrows and the cursor clamp were all written
59	// out in table.go; they are the component's now. What is left is the one thing
60	// this view knows and it does not: which level the table is showing.
61	func (m *Model) updateTableRows() {
62		m.table.SetItems(m.currentItems())
63	}
64	
65	// currentItems returns the children of the current drill-down group (or root nodes)
66	func (m Model) currentItems() []*TreeNode {
67		if m.currentGroupNode == nil {
68			return m.nodes
69		}
70		if m.currentGroupNode.Children == nil {
71			return nil
72		}
73		return m.currentGroupNode.Children
74	}
75	
76	// handleRefresh handles r key
77	func (m Model) handleRefresh() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
78		m.loading = true
79		m.nodes = []*TreeNode{}
80		m.currentGroupNode = nil
81		m.navigationStack = nil
82		m.cursorStack = nil
83		m.activeTabIndex = 0
84		m.table.SetItems(nil)
85		return m, tea.Batch(m.spinner.Tick, m.loadRootGroups())
86	}
87	
88	// handleChildrenLoaded handles ChildrenLoadedMsg
89	func (m Model) handleChildrenLoaded(msg ChildrenLoadedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
90		msg.ParentNode.Children = msg.Children
91		msg.ParentNode.Expanded = true
92		msg.ParentNode.Loading = false
93		m.loading = false
94	
95		m.updateTableRows()
96		m.table.GotoTop()
97	
98		// Continue expanding if there's a pending path
99		if m.pendingSelectPath != "" {
100			return m.expandToPath(m.pendingSelectPath)
101		}
102	
103		return m, nil
104	}
105	
106	// handleLoadError handles LoadErrorMsg
107	func (m Model) handleLoadError(msg LoadErrorMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
108		m.loading = false
109		m.firstLoadDone = true
110		m.error = msg.Error.Error()
111		if msg.ParentNode != nil {
112			msg.ParentNode.Loading = false
113		}
114		return m, nil
115	}
116	
117	// expandToPath navigates to and selects a node at the given path after refresh
118	func (m Model) expandToPath(targetPath string) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
119		// Check if the target is on screen. The rows, not currentItems(): under a
120		// filter or a non-default sort those are two different orderings, and the
121		// cursor indexes the one being shown.
122		for i, node := range m.table.Visible() {
123			if node.FullPath == targetPath {
124				m.table.SetCursor(i)
125				m.pendingSelectPath = ""
126				return m, nil
127			}
128		}
129	
130		// Find an ancestor that needs to be drilled into
131		for _, node := range m.currentItems() {
132			if node.Type == NodeTypeGroup && strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, node.FullPath+"/") {
133				// Drill into this group
134				m.navigationStack = append(m.navigationStack, m.currentGroupNode)
135				m.currentGroupNode = node
136	
137				if node.Children == nil {
138					node.Loading = true
139					m.updateTableRows()
140					return m, m.loadChildren(node)
141				}
142				node.Expanded = true
143				m.updateTableRows()
144				return m.expandToPath(targetPath)
145			}
146		}
147	
148		// Could not find path - clear pending and stay where we are
149		m.pendingSelectPath = ""
150		return m, nil
151	}

### 3.16 The explorer clones, workspaces syncs — **designed, not started**

`p` on a group or a project in the explorer clones the subtree into a
workspace. It works, and it was the least designed path in the application: a
single `Cmd` covering the whole subtree behind a modal showing `"Pulling..."`,
which on a large group is several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze —
observed, not theorised.

The design below came out of a brainstorm. What is settled is settled; the open
questions are marked as such.

#### Settled

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What the explorer does | **Clones what is missing.** A repository already on disk is skipped untouched. |
| 2 | What updates an existing clone | **Nothing here** — a `sync` feature in the workspaces view (§3.17). A dirty working copy is a property of a working copy, so it belongs to the view that owns what is on disk. |
| 3 | The name | **Clone, not Pull.** It was never the behaviour that was wrong, only the label; `pull` is freed for §3.17. |
| 4 | Disk layout | **Mirror from the forge root** under the target directory. |
| 5 | Target directory | **Keep borrowing the workspaces view**, as today. |
| 6 | `gitlab.pull.target_dir` | **Deleted** — done, see below. |
| 7 | Discovery and cloning | **Pipelined.** The list fills as discovery finds repositories and a row starts spinning as soon as it is found. |
| 8 | Selection | A new mode: **several roots at once** — parent folders *and* individual projects — confirmed in one go. |
| 9 | Modals | **Yes/no confirmations only** (Rule 112). The list is the progress view and the report. |
| 10 | Selecting a group | **Takes everything under it.** Drill in to deselect what you do not want. |
| 11 | How a selection is stored | **Roots plus exclusions**, never a positive list of repositories. |
| 12 | Cancelling | **Stops the pipeline, never a clone.** Discovery is cancelled and no new clone is issued; the ones running are awaited. |

| 6 | `gitlab.pull.target_dir` | **Deleted** — done, see below. |
| 7 | Discovery and cloning | **Pipelined.** The list fills as discovery finds repositories and a row starts spinning as soon as it is found. |
| 8 | Selection | A new mode: **several roots at once** — parent folders *and* individual projects — confirmed in one go. |
| 9 | Modals | **Yes/no confirmations only** (Rule 112). The list is the progress view and the report. |
| 10 | Selecting a group | **Takes everything under it.** Drill in to deselect what you do not want. |
| 11 | How a selection is stored | **Roots plus exclusions**, never a positive list of repositories. |
| 12 | Cancelling | **Stops the pipeline, never a clone.** Discovery is cancelled and no new clone is issued; the ones running are awaited. |
| 13 | The list afterwards | **Discarded on `esc`.** The result is what workspaces shows; there is nothing to keep. |
| 14 | The selection control | **No change to `datatable`.** The view supplies the check state through the `Cell` seam that already exists. |

Decision 2 is the load-bearing one. It draws a line that holds: **the explorer
creates what does not exist, workspaces reconciles what does.** The explorer
then never needs to know what a dirty working tree is, and the per-row states
collapse to five — to clone, cloning, cloned, already present, failed.

Decision 4 is what decision 8 forces. Today `nodeSlug` keeps only the **last
segment** of `FullPath` (`tree.go:69-72`), so `acme/platform/backend` pulled
into `~/ws` lands at `~/ws/backend`. With several groups selected at once,
`acme/platform` and `other/platform` would both land on `~/ws/platform` and
silently merge. Mirroring the full path from the forge root cannot collide and
matches what the explorer shows.

Decision 7 is the one that answers the freeze. Building a complete list first
means walking the whole tree through the API before anything happens, which
just moves the dead screen one step earlier. Pipelining removes it entirely, at
the cost of the total only being known at the end — the header counts up
(`47 found…`) instead of announcing a total. Reviewing the full list before
anything starts is given up deliberately; selecting the groups is the act of
decision.

Decision 11 is forced by decision 7, and this is the part worth keeping. A
**positive** list of the chosen repositories cannot be built when a group is
ticked without enumerating its children first — which is the full API walk, run
at selection time. That is the freeze pipelining was chosen to remove, moved one
screen earlier. **Roots plus exclusions represents "this group, minus these"
without knowing what the group contains**, so nothing has to be discovered
before the user confirms. It is the only representation compatible with
decision 7. `RegistryBrowser` already stores its selection as the entries that
were *un*checked (`registry_browser.go:201-202`) — same shape, weaker reason.

Three things fall out of it:

- **The tri-state needs no discovery.** A group renders `CheckSome` exactly when
  some exclusion path is a descendant of it, which is known by construction: an
  exclusion is only ever created by a keystroke on a node already on screen. So
  a group nobody has expanded still displays correctly.
  `theme.CheckState` and `theme.RenderCheckboxTri` already exist and are shared,
  not browser-local.
- **Deselection costs only what it inspects.** Drilling into a group to untick
  something fetches that one level — the lazy navigation that already exists.
- **The overlap question disappears.** Ticking a group and then a descendant is
  meaningless, because the descendant is already implied; unticking makes an
  exclusion and re-ticking removes it. There is no ambiguous case left to rule
  on.

What has to be accepted: **the confirmation screen cannot state a repository
count** — only `3 groups · 1 project · 4 exclusions`. The number appears as
discovery runs, which is the same trade decision 7 already made.

Keys fit Rule 135 unchanged: `←→` drills, `Space` toggles, each keeping one job.

Decision 5 costs nothing: `openBrowser` replaces only `views[ViewWorkspaces]`
and never drops the explorer (`selection.go:37-41`), so a multi-selection in
progress survives the round trip the way `pullTargetNode` does today, and
`PullSelectionCancelledMsg` already returns without losing it.

Decision 12 dissolves the partial-directory question rather than answering it:
a clone is never interrupted, so it never leaves half a repository behind. It
does require **two cancellation scopes**, which is the part to get right.
Discovery is HTTP reads and cancels through a `context` safely; a clone is a
`git clone` writing into a directory, and a `context` that kills it recreates
exactly the mess this decision avoids. So the context covers discovery, and the
scheduler simply stops issuing work.

The cost is that **cancelling is not instant** — up to `ParallelJobs` clones
keep running, which on large repositories is visible. The view has to say so
(`cancelling — 3 clones finishing`), or `esc` reads as ignored. A second `esc`
must not force: forcing is the partial directory, back again.

Decision 13 holds for the successes, which workspaces lists. It loses the
**failures**: a clone that failed wrote nothing, so nothing on disk records it.
That is acceptable because re-running the same selection is self-correcting —
what exists is skipped, what is missing is retried — but the failures must still
reach `log.Printf` and the footer (Rule 128) while the view is alive, or a user
who looks away for three minutes never learns that three repositories failed.

Decision 14 was expected to be the one piece of real work left and turned out
not to be. `Column[T].Cell` is a `func(T) string` the view supplies, so a column
rendering a checkbox glyph computed from the exclusion set is expressible today;
`Update` is a whitelist switch with no `default`, so `Space` is never consumed
and reaches the view. It is the same seam as `SelectedStyles`, for the same
stated reason — the package does not learn what a selection is any more than it
learned what a severity is.

The state must **not** move into `datatable`: `SetItems` replaces the items on
every drill-down, while the selection spans levels the table has never shown. A
selection kept there would be lost on the first `→`.

The real cost sits in the explorer. Columns are built once in `New` and cannot
reach the live model, so the check state has to be carried on a **row type** —
the `imageRow` pattern — moving the table from `Model[*TreeNode]` to
`Model[explorerRow]`. Mechanical, but not free. And `RenderCheckboxTri` styles
its output, so it cannot go in a cell (Rule 122); only the raw icons can.

This judgement flips the day a **second** table needs a selection. For one,
generalising into `datatable` would be speculative.

#### Two prerequisites, both defects in their own right — both done

**A lighter fetch for discovery — done.** The recursive walk cost one call for
subgroups plus one for projects per group, plus **two more per project** —
`fetchLastPipelineStatus` and `fetchProjectAccessLevel`. Two hundred
repositories was 400+ calls for a CI status and a role no clone reads.

`listGroupChildren` is now the paginated, undecorated half both callers share;
`discoverGroupChildren` builds nodes from it and decorates nothing, while
`loadChildren` decorates as before. The two are **not** interchangeable, which
is why the clone also stopped writing what it finds onto `node.Children`:
discovery nodes on the tree the view renders would blank the role and CI
columns for every group a clone had passed through.

That write was also **Rule 110** — a `Cmd` assigning a field `Update` reads —
so the race is gone as a side effect rather than as a patch. It was going to be
removed by the rework anyway; the lighter fetch made keeping it actively
harmful, which is what brought it forward.

**Pagination — done.** Every list in `api.go` stopped at the first page, so a
group of 101 projects enumerated 100. With a list on screen the view would have
stated a count and been wrong, which is why this was a prerequisite rather than
a nicety. Fixed ahead of the rework; see D34.

#### What the rework fixes for free

- **Rule 110 — already gone.** `node.Children` was written inside a `Cmd` on
  the same `*TreeNode` values `Update` reads (`navigation.go:24`, `:70`). The
  lighter discovery fetch removed the write, so the rework inherits a walk with
  no shared state to race on.
- **The four unread `gitlab.pull.*` settings are resolved, two each way.**
  `ParallelJobs` becomes how many rows spin at once and `IncludeArchived` a
  discovery filter; `TargetDir` and `MaxDepth` are deleted. Leaving one declared
  and unread is not an outcome.
- **`gitlab.pull.target_dir` is gone.** It duplicated `app.workspaces_dir` —
  same meaning, and defaults differing by a single letter (`~/workspace` against
  `~/workspaces`), so setting the wrong one changed nothing and said nothing.
  Decision 5 leaves it no role at all.
- **`gitlab.pull.max_depth` is gone**, and not merely for being unread. A depth
  bound **contradicts decision 10**: tick a group, have discovery stop at level
  five, and you get less than you asked for with nothing saying so — the silent
  truncation of D34, reintroduced as a feature. Exclusions express the same
  intent precisely: "only the top level" is drilling in and unticking the
  subgroups, which is explicit and visible. Deleting it also removes the name
  clash with §3.6, which settles a *different* `MaxDepth` — the depth a forge
  declares, 1 for GitHub and unbounded for GitLab.

Both removals landed ahead of the rework, being independent of it;
`TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` covers the configs already on disk.

#### Forge neutrality

The mode has to be built on `TreeNode`, not on GitLab vocabulary. §3.6 settles
that the abstraction declares its depth — GitHub is organisations at level 1 and
repositories at level 2 — so selecting "parent folders" means selecting
organisations there, and decision 4 mirrors a path that is simply shallower.
§3.6 also lists `GitLabConfig`, pull settings included, as GitLab-shaped and due
to move; the fate of the three remaining settings should anticipate that.

### 3.17 `sync` in the workspaces view — **not started**

The counterpart to §3.16 decision 2: the explorer creates what is missing,
workspaces reconciles what exists. Updating a clone, and every question about a
dirty working copy, lives here.

**The data already exists.** `workspaces.Entry` carries `GitBranch`,
`GitRemote`, `GitModified`, `GitUntracked`, `GitUnpushed` and `GitUnpulled`, and
`detectGitStatus` (`entry.go:51`) already fills them on every listing. What is
missing is the **action** — fetch, pull, push — not the knowledge. That makes
this much smaller than it sounds.

**But one of those numbers is not trustworthy today.** `GitUnpulled` comes from
`rev-list --count HEAD..@{u}` (`entry.go:90`), and `@{u}` is the *local*
remote-tracking ref, which only moves after a `git fetch` — and nothing in
DevDesk ever fetches. See D35. Sync therefore has to **fetch first and decide
after**, or it offers to reconcile against stale answers.

Open, all of it: whether sync acts on one row or a selection, whether push is in
scope or only pull, and what it does with a dirty tree — refuse and report is
the obvious default, and it is the whole reason this is not in the explorer.

### 3.13 A sortable column keeps room for its sort arrow — **done**

**D33 — the sort arrow was truncated on any column narrower than its own
header plus two.** Reported from use on the inventory's `CRIT` and `HIGH`, which
asked for 5 and rendered `CRIT ▼` into it.

`Column.MinWidth` is the view's statement about the column's *content*.
`titleFor` then appends an arrow to the header, and `solveWidths` knew nothing
about those two cells — so the component silently widened the thing it was
sizing. The fix belongs there rather than in the view: `askFor` reserves
`width(Title) + sortArrowWidth` for any column carrying a `Less`, and the arrow
strings are named constants so the renderer and the solver cannot drift.

Reserved for **every** sortable column, not only the sorted one: reserving on
demand would resize the column each time `.` moved the sort and shift every
column beside it.

Auditing the application afterwards, `CRIT` and `HIGH` are the **only** two
columns the reserve changes — every other sortable column already had the room.
The four count columns were then pinned to one width (`countColumnWidth`), since
the reserve alone would leave `CRIT`/`HIGH` at 6 and `MED`/`LOW` at 5: four
adjacent columns of the same kind, ragged.

`TestTheWidthsAlwaysSumToWhatIsAvailable` gained the inventory's shape, because
raising what a column asks for is another way to push the total past what is
available and Rule 116 has to survive it.

### 3.12 The Secrets tab shows both scanners, and one rule decides where a finding goes — **done**

Found by reviewing the security header after §3.11, and fixed with it. Four
defects, one cause: nothing owned the question "what kind of finding is this?".

**D29 — two classifiers, and three findings fell between them.**
`Result.CountFindings` switched on `Source` alone and sent everything unmatched
to the severity counters; `countFindingsByTab` switched on `Source` plus
`PkgName` plus `Match`. They disagreed on a `trivy` finding with no `PkgName`,
on an undeclared source, and on a `trivy` finding carrying a `Match` — each of
which was **counted in the header and shown in no tab at all**. Same family as
D24, D25 and D26: two copies of a rule, one of them drifted, nothing said so.
`scan.Categorize` is the only rule now, and it switches on the source alone.

**D30 — Trivy's secrets were parsed and dropped.** `TrivyResult.Secrets` and
`TrivySecret` were declared and unmarshalled into; nothing ever ranged over
them. The help claimed "Secret Scan … (Gitleaks + Trivy)" throughout. Same shape
as D27: declared, populated, read by nothing, silent about it. They are read
now, under a source of their own — `trivy-secret`, which is also what let the
classification stop guessing from `Match`.

**D31 — an image scan ran a secret scan and threw it away.** Trivy's default
scanners for an image are `vuln,secret`, and `trivyArgs` passed no `--scanners`
flag for that target type. So every image scan paid for secret detection whose
output was discarded — and would have reported each secret twice once they were
read. The vulnerability stage now says `--scanners vuln` explicitly.

**D32 — `i` on a Trivy secret would have written a fingerprint that matches
nothing.** `.gitleaksignore` is keyed on a Gitleaks fingerprint;
`AddToGitleaksIgnore` falls back to building one from file, rule and line when
the finding has none. With Trivy secrets in the same tab, `i` would have written
that fabrication and reported "Added … to .gitleaksignore" for a line Gitleaks
will never match and Trivy never reads. It is offered for Gitleaks findings only
now, and refused with a reason otherwise (Rule 128, Rule 130).

Gitleaks and Trivy are **not redundant** — one reads git history, the other the
target's content — so both run when `scan.enable_secret` is set, in separate
stages with separate progress rows and separate error messages. Only Trivy's
half applies to an image, which is what gives an image a secret scan at all.

**The security header now carries the context and one count, and nothing else.**
`buildInfoLines` renders exactly seven lines and drops the rest in silence; the
results state sat at exactly seven, so an eighth field would have vanished. The
tool versions answered the dashboard's question, `Filter` read `ALL`
permanently, and `Secrets`/`Licenses` duplicated the tab bar one line below. The
context was the one thing missing, and it is the view where it matters most: the
scan caches are scoped to a context, so identical rows mean different things in
two of them. `parseVersion`, `looksLikeVersion` and `renderSeverityBar` went
with their only caller.

11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
30		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
31	
32		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
33		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
34	)
35	
36	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
37	type Column[T any] struct {
38		Title string
39		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
40		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
41		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
42		MinWidth int
43		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
44		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
45		Flex int
46		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: bubbles/table
47		// truncates with runewidth, which does not understand ANSI, so a styled
48		// string is cut mid-escape and bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122).
49		// Taking a string rather than a styled value is what makes that
50		// unexpressible here.
51		Cell func(T) string
52		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
53		// `.` skips it.
54		Less func(a, b T) bool
55		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
56		// not participate.
57		Search func(T) string
58	}
59	
60	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
61	type Config[T any] struct {
62		Columns []Column[T]
63		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
64		Tokens []components.FilterToken
65		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
66		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
67		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
68		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
69		SortColumn int
70		// SortDesc opens the table on the descending order of SortColumn. It exists
71		// for the count columns, where ascending is the useless end: an inventory
72		// sorted by CRITICAL wants the worst target first, and cycling `.` past
73		// ascending to reach it on every open is not a default.
74		SortDesc bool
75		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
76		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
77		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
78		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
79		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
80		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
81	}
82	
83	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
84	type Model[T any] struct {
85		cfg   Config[T]
86		table table.Model
87		bar   components.FilterBar
88	
89		items []T
90		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
91		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
92		// ordering while the screen shows another.
93		visible []T
94	
95		sortColumn int
96		sortDesc   bool
97		width      int
98	}
99	
100	// New builds a table from its configuration.
101	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
102		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
103		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
104			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
105		}
106		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
107		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
108	
109		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
110		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
111			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
112		}
113	
114		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn, sortDesc: cfg.SortDesc}
115		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
116		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
117		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
118		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
119		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
120			m.sortColumn = -1
121			// A direction with no column to apply it to would put the header arrow
122			// on nothing and make `.` open on descending.
123			m.sortDesc = false
124		}
125		return m
126	}
127	
128	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
129	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
130	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
131	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
132	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
133		m.items = items
134		m.rebuild()
135	}
136	
137	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
138	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
139	
140	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
141	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
142	
143	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
144	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
145	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
146		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
147		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
148			var zero T
149			return zero, false
150		}
151		return m.visible[cursor], true
152	}
153	
154	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
155	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
156	
157	// SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
158	// remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
159	// level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
160	func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
161		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
162			return
163		}
164		m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
165		m.applyStyles()
166	}
167	
168	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
169	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
170	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
171	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() { m.table.GotoTop() }
172	
173	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
174	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
175	
176	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
177	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
178	
179	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
180	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
181	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
182		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
183			return true
184		}
185		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
186			if c.Search != nil {
187				return true
188			}
189		}
190		return false
191	}
192	
193	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
194	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
195	
196	// View renders the table.
197	func (m *Model[T]) View() string { return m.table.View() }
198	
199	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown.
200	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) { m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1)) }
201	
202	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
203	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
204	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
205		m.table.Focus()
206		m.applyStyles()
207	}
208	
209	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
210		m.table.Blur()
211		m.table.SetStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
212	}
213	
214	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
215	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
216	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
217	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
218		m.width = width
219		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
220	
221		cols := m.table.Columns()
222		for i := range cols {
223			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
224			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
225		}
226		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
227		m.bar.Resize(width)
228		if height > 0 {
229			m.SetHeight(height)
230		}
231		m.applyStyles() // the selected row is pinned to this width
232	}
233	
234	// The sort arrows, and what they cost. Named because widths.go has to reserve
235	// room for them: a column's MinWidth is the view's statement about its content,
236	// and it knows nothing about two cells this package appends to the header.
237	const (
238		sortArrowAsc  = " ▲"
239		sortArrowDesc = " ▼"
240	)
241	
242	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
243	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
244		if i != m.sortColumn {
245			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
246		}
247		if m.sortDesc {
248			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowDesc
249		}
250		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + sortArrowAsc
251	}
252	
253	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
254	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
255	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
256	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
257		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
258		if len(sortable) == 0 {
259			return
260		}
261		switch {
262		case m.sortColumn < 0:
263			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
264		case !m.sortDesc:
265			m.sortDesc = true
266		default:
267			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
268		}
269		m.rebuild()
270		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
271	}
272	
273	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
274	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
275	//
276	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
277	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
278	// a branch nothing can ever check.
279	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
280		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
281			return sortable[at+1]
282		}
283		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
284			return -1
285		}
286		return sortable[0]
287	}
288	
289	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
290		var out []int
291		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
292			if c.Less != nil {
293				out = append(out, i)
294			}
295		}
296		return out
297	}
298	
299	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
300	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
301	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
302	
303	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
304	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
305	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
306	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
307		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
308			var cmd tea.Cmd
309			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
310			m.rebuild()
311			return cmd
312		}
313	
314		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
315		if !ok {
316			return nil
317		}
318		switch key.String() {
319		case "/":
320			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
321			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
322			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
323			if !m.Searchable() {
324				return nil
325			}
326			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
327		case ".":
328			m.CycleSort()
329		case "up", "k":
330			m.table.MoveUp(1)
331			m.applyStyles()
332		case "down", "j":
333			m.table.MoveDown(1)
334			m.applyStyles()
335		case "pgup":
336			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
337			m.applyStyles()
338		case "pgdown":
339			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
340			m.applyStyles()
341		case "g", "home":
342			m.table.GotoTop()
343			m.applyStyles()
344		case "G", "end":
345			m.table.GotoBottom()
346			m.applyStyles()
347		}
348		return nil
349	}
350	
351	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
352	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
353		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
354		m.rebuild()
355	}
356	
357	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
358	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
359	
360	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
361	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
362		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
363	
364		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
365		for i, item := range m.visible {
366			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
367			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
368				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
369			}
370			rows[i] = cells
371		}
372		m.table.SetRows(rows)
373	
374		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
375		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
376		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
377		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
378		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
379		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
380		case len(rows) == 0:
381			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
382			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
383			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
384			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
385		case cursor >= len(rows):
386			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
387		case cursor < 0:
388			m.table.SetCursor(0)
389		}
390		m.applyStyles()
391	}
392	
393	// applyStyles asks the view for the styles that go with the selected item.
394	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
395		if !m.table.Focused() {
396			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
397		}
398		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
399		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
400			styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
401		}
402		// Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
403		// in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
404		// counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border by
405		// however much the row's icons disagreed. Padding to a width the row can
406		// never exceed is a no-op when they agree.
407		if m.width > 2 {
408			styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2)
409		}
410		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
411	}
412	
413	// filtered applies the search query and the toggle filters.
414	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
415		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
416		active := m.activeTokens()
417	
418		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
419		for _, item := range m.items {
420			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
421				continue
422			}
423			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
424				continue
425			}
426			out = append(out, item)
427		}
428		return out
429	}
430	
431	func (m *Model[T]) activeTokens() map[string]bool {
432		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
433		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {
434			if m.bar.IsTokenActive(tok.Label) {
435				active[tok.Label] = true
436			}
437		}
438		return active
439	}
440	
441	// matchesQuery tests the query against each searchable column and then against
442	// the row as a whole.
443	//
444	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
445	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
446	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
447	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
448	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
449	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
450		var joined strings.Builder
451		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
452			if c.Search == nil {
453				continue
454			}
455			value := c.Search(item)
456			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
457				return true
458			}
459			if joined.Len() > 0 {
460				joined.WriteByte(' ')
461			}
462			joined.WriteString(value)
463		}
464		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
465	}
466	
467	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
468	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
469	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
470		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
471			return items
472		}
473		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
474		desc := m.sortDesc
475		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
476			if desc {
477				return less(items[j], items[i])
478			}
479			return less(items[i], items[j])
480		})
481		return items
482	}

### 3.16 The explorer clones, workspaces syncs — **designed, not started**

`p` on a group or a project in the explorer clones the subtree into a
workspace. It works, and it was the least designed path in the application: a
single `Cmd` covering the whole subtree behind a modal showing `"Pulling..."`,
which on a large group is several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze —
observed, not theorised.

The design below came out of a brainstorm. What is settled is settled; the open
questions are marked as such.

#### Settled

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What the explorer does | **Clones what is missing.** A repository already on disk is skipped untouched. |
| 2 | What updates an existing clone | **Nothing here** — a `sync` feature in the workspaces view (§3.17). A dirty working copy is a property of a working copy, so it belongs to the view that owns what is on disk. |
| 3 | The name | **Clone, not Pull.** It was never the behaviour that was wrong, only the label; `pull` is freed for §3.17. |
| 4 | Disk layout | **Mirror from the forge root** under the target directory. |
| 5 | Target directory | **Keep borrowing the workspaces view**, as today. |
| 6 | `gitlab.pull.target_dir` | **Deleted** — done, see below. |
| 7 | Discovery and cloning | **Pipelined.** The list fills as discovery finds repositories and a row starts spinning as soon as it is found. |
| 8 | Selection | A new mode: **several roots at once** — parent folders *and* individual projects — confirmed in one go. |
| 9 | Modals | **Yes/no confirmations only** (Rule 112). The list is the progress view and the report. |
| 10 | Selecting a group | **Takes everything under it.** Drill in to deselect what you do not want. |
| 11 | How a selection is stored | **Roots plus exclusions**, never a positive list of repositories. |
| 12 | Cancelling | **Stops the pipeline, never a clone.** Discovery is cancelled and no new clone is issued; the ones running are awaited. |
| 13 | The list afterwards | **Discarded on `esc`.** The result is what workspaces shows; there is nothing to keep. |
| 14 | The selection control | **No change to `datatable`.** The view supplies the check state through the `Cell` seam that already exists. |

Decision 2 is the load-bearing one. It draws a line that holds: **the explorer
creates what does not exist, workspaces reconciles what does.** The explorer
then never needs to know what a dirty working tree is, and the per-row states
collapse to five — to clone, cloning, cloned, already present, failed.

Decision 4 is what decision 8 forces. Today `nodeSlug` keeps only the **last
segment** of `FullPath` (`tree.go:69-72`), so `acme/platform/backend` pulled
into `~/ws` lands at `~/ws/backend`. With several groups selected at once,
`acme/platform` and `other/platform` would both land on `~/ws/platform` and
silently merge. Mirroring the full path from the forge root cannot collide and
matches what the explorer shows.

Decision 7 is the one that answers the freeze. Building a complete list first
means walking the whole tree through the API before anything happens, which
just moves the dead screen one step earlier. Pipelining removes it entirely, at
the cost of the total only being known at the end — the header counts up
(`47 found…`) instead of announcing a total. Reviewing the full list before
anything starts is given up deliberately; selecting the groups is the act of
decision.

Decision 11 is forced by decision 7, and this is the part worth keeping. A
**positive** list of the chosen repositories cannot be built when a group is
ticked without enumerating its children first — which is the full API walk, run
at selection time. That is the freeze pipelining was chosen to remove, moved one
screen earlier. **Roots plus exclusions represents "this group, minus these"
without knowing what the group contains**, so nothing has to be discovered
before the user confirms. It is the only representation compatible with
decision 7. `RegistryBrowser` already stores its selection as the entries that
were *un*checked (`registry_browser.go:201-202`) — same shape, weaker reason.

Three things fall out of it:

- **The tri-state needs no discovery.** A group renders `CheckSome` exactly when
  some exclusion path is a descendant of it, which is known by construction: an
  exclusion is only ever created by a keystroke on a node already on screen. So
  a group nobody has expanded still displays correctly.
  `theme.CheckState` and `theme.RenderCheckboxTri` already exist and are shared,
  not browser-local.
- **Deselection costs only what it inspects.** Drilling into a group to untick
  something fetches that one level — the lazy navigation that already exists.
- **The overlap question disappears.** Ticking a group and then a descendant is
  meaningless, because the descendant is already implied; unticking makes an
  exclusion and re-ticking removes it. There is no ambiguous case left to rule
  on.

What has to be accepted: **the confirmation screen cannot state a repository
count** — only `3 groups · 1 project · 4 exclusions`. The number appears as
discovery runs, which is the same trade decision 7 already made.

Keys fit Rule 135 unchanged: `←→` drills, `Space` toggles, each keeping one job.

Decision 5 costs nothing: `openBrowser` replaces only `views[ViewWorkspaces]`
and never drops the explorer (`selection.go:37-41`), so a multi-selection in
progress survives the round trip the way `pullTargetNode` does today, and
`PullSelectionCancelledMsg` already returns without losing it.

Decision 12 dissolves the partial-directory question rather than answering it:
a clone is never interrupted, so it never leaves half a repository behind. It
does require **two cancellation scopes**, which is the part to get right.
Discovery is HTTP reads and cancels through a `context` safely; a clone is a

### 3.16 The explorer clones, workspaces syncs — **designed, not started**

`p` on a group or a project in the explorer clones the subtree into a
workspace. It works, and it was the least designed path in the application: a
single `Cmd` covering the whole subtree behind a modal showing `"Pulling..."`,
which on a large group is several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze —
observed, not theorised.

The design below came out of a brainstorm. What is settled is settled; the open
questions are marked as such.

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | What the explorer does | **Clones what is missing.** A repository already on disk is skipped untouched. |
| 2 | What updates an existing clone | **Nothing here** — a `sync` feature in the workspaces view (§3.17). A dirty working copy is a property of a working copy, so it belongs to the view that owns what is on disk. |
| 3 | The name | **Clone, not Pull.** It was never the behaviour that was wrong, only the label; `pull` is freed for §3.17. |
| 4 | Disk layout | **Mirror from the forge root** under the target directory. |
| 5 | Target directory | **Keep borrowing the workspaces view**, as today. |
| 6 | `gitlab.pull.target_dir` | **Deleted** — done, see below. |
| 7 | Discovery and cloning | **Pipelined.** The list fills as discovery finds repositories and a row starts spinning as soon as it is found. |
| 8 | Selection | A new mode: **several roots at once** — parent folders *and* individual projects — confirmed in one go. |
| 9 | Modals | **Yes/no confirmations only** (Rule 112). The list is the progress view and the report. |
| 10 | Selecting a group | **Takes everything under it.** Drill in to deselect what you do not want. |
| 11 | How a selection is stored | **Roots plus exclusions**, never a positive list of repositories. |
| 12 | Cancelling | **Stops the pipeline, never a clone.** Discovery is cancelled and no new clone is issued; the ones running are awaited. |
| 13 | The list afterwards | **Discarded on `esc`.** The result is what workspaces shows; there is nothing to keep. |
| 14 | The selection control | **No change to `datatable`.** The view supplies the check state through the `Cell` seam that already exists. |

matches what the explorer shows.

- **`gitlab.pull.max_depth` is gone**, and not merely for being unread. A depth
  bound **contradicts decision 10**: tick a group, have discovery stop at level

  truncation of D34, reintroduced as a feature. Exclusions express the same
  intent precisely: "only the top level" is drilling in and unticking the
  subgroups, which is explicit and visible. Deleting it also removes the name
  clash with §3.6, which settles a *different* `MaxDepth` — the depth a forge
  declares, 1 for GitHub and unbounded for GitLab.

`TestAConfigCarryingRetiredKeysStillLoads` covers the configs already on disk.

The mode has to be built on `TreeNode`, not on GitLab vocabulary. §3.6 settles
that the abstraction declares its depth — GitHub is organisations at level 1 and
repositories at level 2 — so selecting "parent folders" means selecting
organisations there, and decision 4 mirrors a path that is simply shallower.
§3.6 also lists `GitLabConfig`, pull settings included, as GitLab-shaped and due
to move; the fate of the three remaining settings should anticipate that.

1	package app

3	import (
4		"log"

11	)
12	
13	// Selection mode lets one view borrow another to pick something. The router
14	// remembers where to come back to and delivers the answer.
15	//
16	// There were two borrowers: the security form, which borrowed the workspaces
17	// view for a directory and the images view for an image, and the explorer, which
18	// borrows the workspaces view for a clone destination. The form is gone
19	// (phase 3) — a scan target is a row of the security inventory now — so the
20	// explorer is the only borrower left, and only the workspaces view is ever lent.
21	// That is why nothing here is parameterised any more.
22	
23	// pullDestinationPrompt is shown while the explorer borrows the workspaces view.
24	const pullDestinationPrompt = "Enter into a parent directory — the repo will be cloned inside it"
25	
26	// handleExplorerPullRequest borrows the workspaces view to pick a clone target.
27	func (a *App) handleExplorerPullRequest() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
28		a.selectionReturnView = a.currentView
29		log.Printf("Explorer pull request: switching to workspaces for directory selection")
30		return a, a.openBrowser(
31			command.ViewWorkspaces,
32			workspaces.NewForSelection(a.config, pullDestinationPrompt),
33		)
34	}
35	
36	// openBrowser installs a view built in selection mode and lays it out.
37	func (a *App) openBrowser(view command.ViewType, model tea.Model) tea.Cmd {
38		a.views[view] = model
39		a.currentView = view
40		return tea.Batch(model.Init(), a.requestResize())
41	}
42	
43	// handleDirectorySelected returns to the explorer with the chosen path.
44	func (a *App) handleDirectorySelected(msg workspaces.DirectorySelectedMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
45		log.Printf("Directory selected: %s, returning to %s", msg.Path, a.selectionReturnView)
46		a.leaveSelectionMode()
47		return a, a.returnToOrigin(explorer.PullDestinationSelectedMsg{Path: msg.Path})
48	}
49	
50	// handleSelectionCancelled returns to the explorer without changes.
51	func (a *App) handleSelectionCancelled() (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
52		log.Printf("Selection cancelled, returning to %s", a.selectionReturnView)
53		a.leaveSelectionMode()
54		return a, a.returnToOrigin(explorer.PullSelectionCancelledMsg{})
55	}
56	
57	// leaveSelectionMode drops the workspaces view so it is rebuilt normally.
58	func (a *App) leaveSelectionMode() {
59		a.currentView = a.selectionReturnView
60		delete(a.views, command.ViewWorkspaces)
61	}
62	
63	// returnToOrigin delivers the outcome to the view that asked and lays it out.
64	func (a *App) returnToOrigin(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
65		view, ok := a.views[a.currentView]
66		if !ok {
67			return nil
68		}
69		updatedView, cmd := view.Update(msg)
70		a.views[a.currentView] = updatedView
71		a.viewport.GotoTop()
72		return tea.Batch(cmd, a.requestResize())
73	}

feat: the explorer clones what you select (§3.16)

`p` on a group cloned its subtree behind a modal reading "Pulling...", which on
a large group is several minutes indistinguishable from a freeze. The three
blocks the design called for, together:

**explorerRow.** The table moves from `Model[*TreeNode]` to `Model[explorerRow]`.
Columns are built once in `New` and close over nothing, so a decoration that
changes with a keystroke has to travel on the row — the `imageRow` pattern.
`selectedNode()` keeps every action reading a node, as before.

**The selection mode.** `c` opens the tree with a checkbox on the Type cell;
`space` ticks, `←→` still drill, `enter` confirms. The selection is roots plus
exclusions (decision 11), so ticking a group needs no discovery — which is what
lets discovery start only after the user has confirmed. The checkbox rides on
the Type cell rather than taking a column: a column would cost four cells on
every screen to say nothing on all but one of them.

**The pipeline.** Discovery feeds a pool of `ParallelJobs` clones, and a
repository becomes a row the moment it is found. `esc` cancels discovery and
stops the scheduler issuing work, but never interrupts a `git clone` — killing
one leaves half a repository on disk, which is the mess decision 12 avoids. A
second `esc` therefore does nothing until the run ends.

Also settled by the rework:

- The destination mirrors the forge path in full (decision 4). Keeping only the
  last segment made `acme/platform` and `other/platform` land on one directory
  and merge — impossible while one subtree was cloned at a time, possible now
  that several roots are confirmed at once.
- `gitlab.pull.include_archived` is read, by `listGroupChildren`. Browsing still
  lists everything; only a clone filters.
- `components.ReportModal` is gone with its one caller. Modals are yes/no
  confirmations again (decision 9, Rule 112).

The failures are named in the footer and the log when the run ends: decision 13
discards the list, workspaces records only the successes, and a clone that
failed wrote nothing at all.
MSG
